--- Where a point sits inside an object, as a 0..1 pair, corrected for the
--- space it was reported in. Returns nil when the point is outside it.
local function Locate(Space, Point, Object)
	local Origin = Object.AbsolutePosition
	local Size = Object.AbsoluteSize

	if Size.X <= 0 or Size.Y <= 0 then
		return nil
	end

	local Correction = Shift(Space)

	local X = (Point.X + Correction.X - Origin.X) / Size.X
	local Y = (Point.Y + Correction.Y - Origin.Y) / Size.Y

	if X < 0 or X > 1 or Y < 0 or Y > 1 then
		return nil
	end

	return X, Y
end

--- Pointer dragging over a surface, reported as a 0..1 fraction of it. The
--- move and end handlers are global so a drag survives leaving the target.
local function Draggable(Target, Surface, OnMove, OnEnd)
	local Connections = {}
	local Dragging = false

	local function Report(Point)
		local Origin = Surface.AbsolutePosition
		local Size = Surface.AbsoluteSize
		local Correction = Shift("Input")

		OnMove(
			Size.X > 0 and Clamp((Point.X + Correction.X - Origin.X) / Size.X, 0, 1) or 0,
			Size.Y > 0 and Clamp((Point.Y + Correction.Y - Origin.Y) / Size.Y, 0, 1) or 0
		)
	end

	table.insert(Connections, Target.InputBegan:Connect(function(Input)
		if Input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1
			or Input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch then
			Dragging = true

			--- The press fired on this object, so it landed inside it. That is
			--- the one free measurement of the gap we ever get.
			Learn("Input", Input.Position, Target)

			Report(Input.Position)
		end
	end))

	table.insert(Connections, UserInputService.InputChanged:Connect(function(Input)
		if Dragging and (Input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseMovement
			or Input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch) then
			Report(Input.Position)
		end
	end))

	table.insert(Connections, UserInputService.InputEnded:Connect(function(Input)
		if Dragging and (Input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1
			or Input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch) then
			Dragging = false

			if OnEnd then
				OnEnd()
			end
		end
	end))

	return function()
		for _, Connection in Connections do
			Connection:Disconnect()
		end

		table.clear(Connections)
	end
end

--- One tooltip for the whole library, moved and refilled rather than rebuilt.
local Tip = nil
local TipTrack = nil

local function Tooltip(Object, Content)
	local function Ensure()
		if Tip and Tip.Parent then
			return Tip
		end

		Tip = New("Frame", {
			Name                   = "Tooltip",
			Parent                 = Screen.Get(),
			BackgroundColor3       = Theme.Scrim,
			BackgroundTransparency = 0.08,
			BorderSizePixel        = 0,
			AnchorPoint            = Vector2.new(0, 1),
			AutomaticSize          = Enum.AutomaticSize.XY,
			Size                   = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0),
			Visible                = false,
			ZIndex                 = 90,
		}, {
			Corner(Metrics.ChipRadius),
			Padding(5, 9),
			Stroke(Theme.White, 0.82, 1),
		})

		Text({
			Parent           = Tip,
			Name             = "Label",
			Text             = "",
			TextSize         = Metrics.ValueSize,
			TextTransparency = Theme.TextSecondary,
			AutomaticSize    = Enum.AutomaticSize.XY,
			Size             = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0),
			ZIndex           = 91,
		})

		return Tip
	end

	local Connections = {}

	table.insert(Connections, Object.MouseEnter:Connect(function()
		local Frame = Ensure()

		Frame.Label.Text = Content
		Frame.Visible = true
		Frame.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		Frame.Label.TextTransparency = 1

		TipTrack = Object

		Tween(Frame, { BackgroundTransparency = 0.08 }, "hint")
		Tween(Frame.Label, { TextTransparency = Theme.TextSecondary }, "hint")

		local Point = Object.AbsolutePosition
		Frame.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(Point.X, Point.Y - 4)
	end))

	table.insert(Connections, Object.MouseLeave:Connect(function()
		if Tip and TipTrack == Object then
			Tip.Visible = false
			TipTrack = nil
		end
	end))

	return function()
		for _, Connection in Connections do
			Connection:Disconnect()
		end
	end
end

--- Everything every handle can do, mixed in once rather than written forty
--- times. Controls add their own Get/Set on top.
local function Common(Handle, Frame, Options, Bits)
	Bits = Bits or {}
	Options = Options or {}

	local Disabled = Options.Disabled == true
	local Cleanup = {}

	Handle.Frame = Frame
	Handle.Options = Options

	function Handle:IsVisible()
		return Frame.Visible
	end

	--- Hiding a row also has to take it out of the layout, which Visible
	--- already does, so this is genuinely just the property — but it belongs
	--- on the handle so callers never reach through to the instance.
	function Handle:SetVisible(Value, Animate)
		if Animate and Value then
			Frame.Visible = true
			Enter(Frame, "BackgroundTransparency", Frame.BackgroundTransparency, "fade")
		else
			Frame.Visible = Value ~= false
		end

		return Handle
	end

	function Handle:IsDisabled()
		return Disabled
	end

	--- Disabled dims the whole row and stops it taking input. Controls that
	--- own extra buttons pass them in Bits.Inputs.
	function Handle:SetDisabled(Value)
		Disabled = Value ~= false

		Tween(Frame, { BackgroundTransparency = Disabled
			and 1
			or (Options.Flat and 1 or Theme.RowTransparency) }, "fade")

		for _, Object in Bits.Inputs or {} do
			Object.Active = not Disabled
			Object.Selectable = not Disabled
			Object.AutoButtonColor = false
		end

		for _, Object in Bits.Dim or {} do
			if Object:IsA("TextLabel") or Object:IsA("TextButton") or Object:IsA("TextBox") then
				Tween(Object, { TextTransparency = Disabled and Theme.TextDisabled or Theme.TextSecondary }, "fade")
			elseif Object:IsA("ImageLabel") or Object:IsA("ImageButton") then
				Tween(Object, { ImageTransparency = Disabled and Theme.TextDisabled or 0 }, "fade")
			end
		end

		return Handle
	end

	if Bits.Label then
		function Handle:SetLabel(NewText)
			SwapText(Bits.Label, NewText)
			return Handle
		end
	end

	if Bits.Description then
		function Handle:SetDescription(NewText)
			SwapText(Bits.Description, NewText)
			return Handle
		end
	end

	local function Teardown()
		for _, Stop in Cleanup do
			Stop()
		end

		table.clear(Cleanup)

		if Bits.Destroy then
			Bits.Destroy()
		end

		Frame:Destroy()
	end

	--- Destroy is immediate, because most of the time something is being torn
	--- down and nobody is watching. Pass true and it shrinks and fades out
	--- first — asked for explicitly, since a control that lingers after the
	--- code that removed it has moved on is a bug in every other case.
	function Handle:Destroy(Animate)
		if not Animate or not Frame.Parent then
			Teardown()
			return
		end

		--- Taken out of the layout the instant it starts leaving, so the rows
		--- underneath close the gap while it goes rather than after.
		Frame.Active = false
		Motion.Out(Frame, Teardown)
	end

	function Handle:OnDestroy(Stop)
		table.insert(Cleanup, Stop)
		return Handle
	end

	if Options.Tooltip then
		table.insert(Cleanup, Tooltip(Frame, Options.Tooltip))
	end

	if Options.Visible == false then
		Frame.Visible = false
	end

	--- Anything built while the interface is already up can arrive rather than
	--- appear. Off by default: a page of forty rows should not each spring in
	--- on their own, which is what Stagger is for.
	if Options.Enter then
		Motion.Pop(Frame, type(Options.Enter) == "string" and Options.Enter or "pop")
		Enter(Frame, "BackgroundTransparency", Frame.BackgroundTransparency, "fade")
	end

	--- Or it can arrive as a white plate that becomes it. The measurement has
	--- to wait for a layout pass, because a control has no size on the frame it
	--- is built.
	if Options.Reveal then
		task.defer(function()
			if Frame.Parent then
				require(script.Parent.Reveal).Plate(Frame, {
					From   = type(Options.Reveal) == "table" and Options.Reveal.From or nil,
					Radius = Util.Radius(Options, Metrics.RowRadius),
				})
			end
		end)
	end

	if Disabled then
		task.defer(function()
			Handle:SetDisabled(true)
		end)
	end

	return Handle
end

--- Surface variants. Every shell resolves through here, so "Outline" means the
--- same thing on a row, a block and an alert.
local function Dress(Frame, Options, Fallback, Against)
	local Variant = Options.Variant or (Options.Flat and "Flat") or Fallback or "Filled"
	local Colour = Options.Color

	if Variant == "Flat" or Variant == "Ghost" then
		Frame.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	elseif Variant == "Outline" then
		Frame.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		Stroke(Colour or Theme.White, 0.7, 1).Parent = Frame
	elseif Variant == "Solid" then
		Frame.BackgroundColor3 = Colour or Theme.White
		Frame.BackgroundTransparency = 0.86
	elseif Variant == "Rule" then
		Frame.BackgroundTransparency = 1

		local Accent = New("Frame", {
			Name             = "Accent",
			Parent           = Frame,
			BackgroundColor3 = Colour or Theme.White,
			BackgroundTransparency = Theme.RuleTransparency,
			BorderSizePixel  = 0,
			Size             = UDim2.new(0, 1, Against and 0 or 1, 0),
			ZIndex           = 3,
		})

		if Against then
			Span(Accent, Against, true)
		end
	else
		Frame.BackgroundColor3 = Theme.White
		Frame.BackgroundTransparency = Theme.RowTransparency
	end

	return Variant
end

--- Whether a variant reacts to the pointer at all.
local function Reactive(Variant)
	return Variant ~= "Flat" and Variant ~= "Ghost" and Variant ~= "Outline"
end

--- A line: label and description on the left, a mount on the right.
---
--- The whole thing is AutomaticSize.Y with a minimum, so a long description
--- grows the row rather than spilling out of it — which is what happens as
--- soon as anyone raises RowDescSize.
local function Row(Parent, Options)
	Options = Options or {}

	local HasDescription = Options.Description ~= nil and Options.Description ~= ""
	local Reserve = Options.Reserve or Metrics.ToggleWidth
	local Pad = Options.Padding or Metrics.RowPadding

	--- The row's root is a button, not a frame.
	---
	--- Almost every control wants the whole row to be clickable, and the
	--- obvious way — a full size TextButton on top — cannot work here: the row
	--- is laid out by a UIListLayout, which lays out every visible child it
	--- has, so the cover became a list item as tall as the row it was covering.
	--- Making the root itself the button removes the extra child entirely.
	local Frame = New("TextButton", {
		Name                   = Options.Name or "Row",
		Parent                 = Parent,
		BackgroundColor3       = Theme.White,
		BackgroundTransparency = Theme.RowTransparency,
		BorderSizePixel        = 0,
		Text                   = "",
		AutoButtonColor        = false,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0),
		AutomaticSize          = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y,
		LayoutOrder            = Options.LayoutOrder or 0,
	}, {
		Corner(Util.Radius(Options, Metrics.RowRadius)),
		Padding(10, Pad, 10, Pad),
	})

	--- The minimum keeps short rows the height they have always been, so
	--- nothing in a list of toggles jumps around.
	New("UISizeConstraint", {
		Parent  = Frame,
		MinSize = Vector2.new(0, Options.Height
			or (HasDescription and Metrics.RowHeightTall or Metrics.RowHeight)),
	})

	--- The stack carries the layout; the row carries the decoration. Keeping
	--- them apart is what lets a full height accent exist at all: a child of
	--- the row's own layout would be laid out as a list item, and a child
	--- measured against the row would grow it.
	local Stack = New("Frame", {
		Name                   = "Stack",
		Parent                 = Frame,
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0),
		AutomaticSize          = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y,
	}, {
		List(Options.Gap or 8),
	})

	local Variant = Dress(Frame, Options, nil, Stack)

	--- The head is a horizontal layout, not a set of anchored children.
	---
	--- Anchoring a child at 0.5 scale inside an AutomaticSize parent, or giving
	--- one a scale height there, makes the parent's measured height depend on
	--- its own height. Roblox resolves that by growing: rows built that way
	--- came out hundreds of pixels tall. A layout has no such loop.
	local MountHeight = Options.MountHeight or 26

	local Head = New("Frame", {
		Name                   = "Head",
		Parent                 = Stack,
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0),
		AutomaticSize          = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y,
		LayoutOrder            = 1,
	}, {
		New("UIListLayout", {
			Padding             = UDim.new(0, 8),
			FillDirection       = Enum.FillDirection.Horizontal,
			SortOrder           = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder,
			HorizontalAlignment = Enum.HorizontalAlignment.Left,
			VerticalAlignment   = Enum.VerticalAlignment.Center,
		}),
	})

	local Icon = nil

	if Options.Icon then
		Icon = New("ImageLabel", {
			Name                   = "Icon",
			Parent                 = Head,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			Image                  = Util.Asset(Options.Icon),
			ImageColor3            = Options.IconColor or Theme.White,
			ImageTransparency      = Theme.TextSecondary,
			Size                   = UDim2.new(0, 16, 0, 16),
			LayoutOrder            = 1,
		})
	end

	local TextColumn = New("Frame", {
		Name                   = "Text",
		Parent                 = Head,
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(1, -(Reserve + (Icon and 34 or 8)), 0, 0),
		AutomaticSize          = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y,
		LayoutOrder            = 2,
	}, {
		List(2),
	})

	--- A minimum on the column, not on the head: the head is exactly as tall
	--- as the taller of the column and the mount, which is what centres them.
	New("UISizeConstraint", {
		Parent  = TextColumn,
		MinSize = Vector2.new(0, MountHeight),
	})

	local Label = Text({
		Parent           = TextColumn,
		Text             = Options.Label or "",
		TextSize         = Options.LabelSize or Metrics.RowLabelSize,
		TextTransparency = Theme.TextPrimary,
		TextWrapped      = Options.Wrap ~= false,
		LayoutOrder      = 1,
	})

	local Description = nil

	if HasDescription then
		Description = Text({
			Parent           = TextColumn,
			Text             = Options.Description,
			TextSize         = Options.DescriptionSize or Metrics.RowDescSize,
			TextTransparency = Theme.TextSecondary,
			TextWrapped      = true,
			LayoutOrder      = 2,
		})
	end

	--- Fixed height, never scale: the mount is a child of an AutomaticSize
	--- head, and a scale height there is the loop described above.
	local Mount = New("Frame", {
		Name                   = "Mount",
		Parent                 = Head,
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(0, Reserve, 0, MountHeight),
		LayoutOrder            = 3,
		ZIndex                 = 2,
	})

	local Built = {
		Frame       = Frame,
		Stack       = Stack,
		Head        = Head,
		Mount       = Mount,
		Label       = Label,
		Description = Description,
		TextColumn  = TextColumn,
		Icon        = Icon,
		Variant     = Variant,
	}

	--- Widens the mount and narrows the text column to match, which is the
	--- first thing almost every control does.
	function Built:Reserve(Width, Height)
		local Gap = Icon and 34 or 8

		--- Same rule as a Block's aside: in a narrow row the mount takes what
		--- is there rather than what it asked for, so the label keeps a line.
		local function Share()
			local Room = Head.AbsoluteSize.X
			local Taken = Width

			if Room > 0 then
				Taken = math.min(Width, math.max(0, Room * 0.6 - Gap))
			end

			Mount.Size = UDim2.new(0, Taken, 0, Height or MountHeight)
			TextColumn.Size = UDim2.new(1, -(Taken + Gap), 0, 0)
		end

		Built.Share = Share

		--- One connection, however many times a control re-reserves: it always
		--- calls the latest share.
		if not Built.Sharing then
			Built.Sharing = Head:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"):Connect(function()
				Built.Share()
			end)
		end

		Share()

		return Mount
	end

	--- A full width strip under the head, for sliders and anything else that
	--- needs the whole row rather than a corner of it.
	function Built:Foot(Height)
		local Foot = New("Frame", {
			Name                   = "Foot",
			Parent                 = Stack,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, Height or 18),
			LayoutOrder            = 2,
		})

		return Foot
	end

	if Reactive(Variant) and Options.Static ~= true then
		Frame.MouseEnter:Connect(function()
			Tween(Frame, { BackgroundTransparency = Theme.RowHoverTransparency }, "hover")
		end)

		Frame.MouseLeave:Connect(function()
			Tween(Frame, { BackgroundTransparency = Theme.RowTransparency }, "hover")
		end)

		Enter(Frame, "BackgroundTransparency", Theme.RowTransparency, "fade")
	end

	return Built
end

--- A card: optional heading and description, an aside in the top right, and a
--- content area that grows with whatever is put in it.
local function Block(Parent, Options, Height)
	Options = Options or {}

	local Pad = Options.Padding or Metrics.RowPadding

	local Frame = New("Frame", {
		Name                   = Options.Name or "Block",
		Parent                 = Parent,
		BackgroundColor3       = Theme.White,
		BackgroundTransparency = Theme.RowTransparency,
		BorderSizePixel        = 0,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0),
		AutomaticSize          = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y,
		LayoutOrder            = Options.LayoutOrder or 0,
	}, {
		Corner(Util.Radius(Options, Metrics.RowRadius)),
		Padding(12, Pad, 12, Pad),
		List(Options.Gap or 8),
	})

	local Variant = Dress(Frame, Options)

	local Head, Aside = nil, nil

	if Options.Label then
		Head = New("Frame", {
			Name                   = "Head",
			Parent                 = Frame,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0),
			AutomaticSize          = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y,
			LayoutOrder            = 1,
		})

		local Column = New("Frame", {
			Name                   = "Column",
			Parent                 = Head,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			Size                   = UDim2.new(1, -(Options.AsideWidth or 100), 0, 0),
			AutomaticSize          = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y,
		}, {
			List(2),
		})

		Text({
			Parent      = Column,
			Text        = Options.Label,
			TextSize    = Options.LabelSize or Metrics.RowLabelSize,
			TextWrapped = true,
			LayoutOrder = 1,
		})

		if Options.Description and Options.Description ~= "" then
			Text({
				Parent           = Column,
				Text             = Options.Description,
				TextSize         = Options.DescriptionSize or Metrics.RowDescSize,
				TextTransparency = Theme.TextSecondary,
				TextWrapped      = true,
				LayoutOrder      = 2,
			})
		end

		--- Hand positioned, so it never joins the list layout and never grows
		--- the head.
		Aside = New("Frame", {
			Name                   = "Aside",
			Parent                 = Head,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			AnchorPoint            = Vector2.new(1, 0),
			Position               = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 1),
			Size                   = UDim2.new(0, (Options.AsideWidth or 100) - 12, 0, 20),
		})

		--- In a narrow container a fixed aside leaves the label a few pixels to
		--- live in, and a wrapped label turns into one letter per line. The
		--- aside gives ground instead: it never takes more than its share of
		--- the room actually available.
		local Wanted = Options.AsideWidth or 100

		local function Share()
			local Room = Head.AbsoluteSize.X
			local Reserve = Wanted

			if Room > 0 then
				Reserve = math.min(Wanted, math.max(0, Room * (Options.AsideShare or 0.45)))
			end

			Column.Size = UDim2.new(1, -Reserve, 0, 0)
			Aside.Size = UDim2.new(0, math.max(0, Reserve - 12), 0, Options.AsideHeight or 20)
		end

		Head:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"):Connect(Share)
		Share()
	end

	local Content = New("Frame", {
		Name                   = "Content",
		Parent                 = Frame,
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, Height or 0),
		AutomaticSize          = Height and Enum.AutomaticSize.None or Enum.AutomaticSize.Y,
		LayoutOrder            = 2,
	})

	if Reactive(Variant) and Options.Static ~= true then
		Frame.MouseEnter:Connect(function()
			Tween(Frame, { BackgroundTransparency = Theme.RowHoverTransparency }, "hover")
		end)

		Frame.MouseLeave:Connect(function()
			Tween(Frame, { BackgroundTransparency = Theme.RowTransparency }, "hover")
		end)

		Enter(Frame, "BackgroundTransparency", Theme.RowTransparency, "fade")
	end

	return {
		Frame   = Frame,
		Content = Content,
		Head    = Head,
		Aside   = Aside,
		Variant = Variant,
	}
end

--- Charts. A line is drawn as rotated one pixel frames, because Roblox has no
--- primitive for one and this is the cheapest thing that animates.
--- A line drawn as a run of rotated bars, redrawn in place when the data moves.
---
--- The obvious way to animate this is to spring each bar's position, length and
--- angle toward its new value. It looks wrong, and it took seeing it to know
--- why: those three numbers are not independent. A bar is defined by its two
--- endpoints, and springing the derived values separately lets the line come
--- apart in flight — bars detach from their neighbours, swing, and rejoin.
---
--- So the POINTS are what moves. They chase their targets on a plain
--- exponential, every bar is rebuilt from them on each frame, and the line is
--- therefore joined at every instant it is drawn. One frame connection per
--- line, which lets go as soon as it has arrived.
local function Polyline(Parent, Pool, Points, Colour, Alpha, Thickness)
	local Chase = Pool.Chase or 16

	--- The first draw is not an animation: there is nothing to move from.
	if not Pool.Current then
		Pool.Current = {}

		for Index, Point in Points do
			Pool.Current[Index] = Point
		end
	end

	--- A line that has just gained or lost points has nowhere sensible to move
	--- those from, so they start where they belong.
	for Index = #Pool.Current + 1, #Points do
		Pool.Current[Index] = Points[Index]
	end

	for Index = #Points + 1, #Pool.Current do
		Pool.Current[Index] = nil
	end

	Pool.Target = Points
	Pool.Colour = Colour
	Pool.Alpha = Alpha
	Pool.Thickness = Thickness

	local function Draw()
		local Current = Pool.Current
		local Wanted = math.max(0, #Current - 1)

		for Index = 1, Wanted do
			local From, To = Current[Index], Current[Index + 1]
			local Delta = To - From
			local Length = Delta.Magnitude

			local Segment = Pool[Index]

			if not Segment or not Segment.Parent then
				Segment = New("Frame", {
					Name                   = "Segment",
					Parent                 = Parent,
					BackgroundColor3       = Pool.Colour,
					BackgroundTransparency = 1,
					BorderSizePixel        = 0,
					AnchorPoint            = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5),
				})

				Pool[Index] = Segment
				Tween(Segment, { BackgroundTransparency = Pool.Alpha }, "fade")
			else
				Segment.BackgroundColor3 = Pool.Colour
			end

			--- Assigned, not tweened. The motion is in the points; the bars
			--- only ever report where the points currently are.
			Segment.Position = UDim2.fromOffset((From.X + To.X) / 2, (From.Y + To.Y) / 2)
			Segment.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(Length + 1, Pool.Thickness or 1)
			Segment.Rotation = math.deg(math.atan2(Delta.Y, Delta.X))
		end

		for Index = Wanted + 1, #Pool do
			local Segment = Pool[Index]

			if Segment then
				Tween(Segment, { BackgroundTransparency = 1 }, "exit")

				task.delay(MotionTime("exit"), function()
					Segment:Destroy()
				end)

				Pool[Index] = nil
			end
		end
	end

	local function Settled()
		for Index, Point in Pool.Current do
			local Want = Pool.Target[Index]

			if Want and (Want - Point).Magnitude > 0.25 then
				return false
			end
		end

		return true
	end

	local function Sleep()
		if Pool.Driver then
			Pool.Driver:Disconnect()
			Pool.Driver = nil
		end
	end

	if Settled() then
		Pool.Current = Pool.Target
		Draw()
		Sleep()

		return Pool
	end

	if not Pool.Driver then
		Pool.Driver = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(Delta)
			if not Parent.Parent then
				Sleep()
				return
			end

			local Step = 1 - math.exp(-Chase * math.min(Delta, 1 / 20))

			for Index, Point in Pool.Current do
				local Want = Pool.Target[Index]

				if Want then
					Pool.Current[Index] = Point + (Want - Point) * Step
				end
			end

			Draw()

			if Settled() then
				for Index, Want in Pool.Target do
					Pool.Current[Index] = Want
				end

				Draw()
				Sleep()
			end
		end)
	end

	Draw()

	return Pool
end

local function ChartPoints(Values, Width, Height, Minimum, Maximum)
	local Span = Maximum - Minimum
	local Points = {}

	for Index, Value in Values do
		local X = #Values > 1 and (Index - 1) / (#Values - 1) * Width or 0
		local Y = Height - (Span > 0 and (Value - Minimum) / Span or 0.5) * Height

		Points[Index] = Vector2.new(X, Y)
	end

	return Points
end

--- The range a chart is drawn against, honouring explicit bounds and falling
--- back to the data. A flat series is padded so it does not divide by zero.
local function Extent(Values, Options)
	local Minimum = Options.Min
	local Maximum = Options.Max

	if not Minimum or not Maximum then
		local Low, High = math.huge, -math.huge

		for _, Value in Values do
			Low = math.min(Low, Value)
			High = math.max(High, Value)
		end

		if Low == math.huge then
			Low, High = 0, 1
		end

		if Low == High then
			Low, High = Low - 1, High + 1
		end

		Minimum = Minimum or Low
		Maximum = Maximum or High
	end

	return Minimum, Maximum
end

--- The finisher for Block based controls.
local function BlockHandle(Built, Extra, Options)
	local Handle = Extra or {}

	return Common(Handle, Built.Frame, Options or {}, {})
end

Parts.Span        = Span
Parts.Layered     = Layered
Parts.SlidingMark = SlidingMark
Parts.Draggable   = Draggable
Parts.Learn       = Learn
Parts.Locate      = Locate
Parts.Tooltip     = Tooltip
Parts.Common      = Common
Parts.Dress       = Dress
Parts.Row         = Row
Parts.Block       = Block
Parts.BlockHandle = BlockHandle
Parts.Polyline    = Polyline
Parts.ChartPoints = ChartPoints
Parts.Extent      = Extent

return Parts
Reveal:
--!nonstrict
--- Reveal.luau — the white layer.
---
--- Everything in here is one idea: a plain white shape stands in for something
--- for a moment, and then hands over to it. A panel opens as a white plate that
--- grows and dissolves into the real panel. A moving highlight drags a white
--- smear behind it. A line of type is uncovered by a white bar sweeping across
--- it. The white is never decoration — it is always the thing that is about to
--- be there, or the thing that just was.
---
--- The timings are measured, not invented. See MOTION.md for the frame tables
--- they came from; the short version is that the plate grows on one axis, then
--- the other, then dissolves, and the whole gesture is under half a second.

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local Palette = require(script.Parent.Theme)
local Util    = require(script.Parent.Util)
local Motion  = require(script.Parent.Motion)

local Theme   = Palette.Tokens

local New   = Util.New
local Clamp = Util.Clamp

local Tween      = Motion.Tween
local MotionTime = Motion.MotionTime

local Reveal = {}

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Shared
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- The rectangle an object occupies inside a given parent, in offset pixels.
--- Everything here works in offset rather than scale, because a white stand in
--- has to sit exactly on top of a thing whose own size may be in either.
--- A child's offset is measured from the inside of its parent's padding, not
--- from the parent's own corner, so a rectangle worked out from AbsolutePosition
--- alone lands one padding down and to the right of the thing it stands for.
local function Inset(Within)
	local Pad = Within:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("UIPadding")

	if not Pad then
		return 0, 0
	end

	local Size = Within.AbsoluteSize

	return Pad.PaddingLeft.Scale * Size.X + Pad.PaddingLeft.Offset,
		Pad.PaddingTop.Scale * Size.Y + Pad.PaddingTop.Offset
end

local function Rect(Object, Within)
	local Origin = Within.AbsolutePosition
	local Point = Object.AbsolutePosition
	local Size = Object.AbsoluteSize
	local PadX, PadY = Inset(Within)

	return Point.X - Origin.X - PadX, Point.Y - Origin.Y - PadY, Size.X, Size.Y
end

--- A white shape, with the corner and the stroke of whatever it is standing in
--- for, so the stand in does not have a different silhouette to the real thing.
local function Plate(Parent, Options)
	Options = Options or {}

	local Face = New("Frame", {
		Name                   = Options.Name or "Plate",
		Parent                 = Parent,
		BackgroundColor3       = Options.Color or Theme.White,
		BackgroundTransparency = Options.Transparency or 0,
		BorderSizePixel        = 0,
		AnchorPoint            = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5),
		ZIndex                 = Options.ZIndex or 50,
		Active                 = false,
		Selectable             = false,
	})

	if Options.Radius and Options.Radius > 0 then
		Util.Corner(Options.Radius).Parent = Face
	end

	return Face
end

--- Runs something once an object actually has a size.
---
--- Nothing built this frame has been laid out yet, so anything that measures a
--- thing it has only just made measures zero. Every reveal in here refuses a
--- rectangle it cannot measure — which is right, but it meant that revealing a
--- row you had just added did nothing at all, silently.
---
--- So: try now, and if there is nothing to measure yet, wait for the first size
--- the object is given and try again. Callers that need a synchronous answer —
--- a window deciding whether to fall back to a plain fade — pass Now and get
--- the old behaviour.
local function Ready(Object, Run)
	if not Object or not Object.Parent then
		return function() end
	end

	if Object.AbsoluteSize.X >= 2 and Object.AbsoluteSize.Y >= 1 then
		Run()
		return function() end
	end

	local Watch = nil
	local Done = false

	local function Go()
		if Done or not Object.Parent then
			return
		end

		if Object.AbsoluteSize.X < 2 or Object.AbsoluteSize.Y < 1 then
			return
		end

		Done = true

		if Watch then
			Watch:Disconnect()
			Watch = nil
		end

		Run()
	end

	Watch = Object:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"):Connect(Go)

	task.defer(Go)

	return function()
		Done = true

		if Watch then
			Watch:Disconnect()
			Watch = nil
		end
	end
end

Reveal.Ready = Ready

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The plate reveal
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- A panel arriving as a white plate.
---
--- The choreography, measured off the reference footage frame by frame at 24fps
--- and then fitted. Reference on the left, what this produces on the right:
---
---   frame   width  height  alpha      width  height  alpha
---     1      221     149    0.60       220     148    0.60
---     2      349     149    0.89       357     148    0.92
---     3      391     164    0.96       390     148    0.99
---     4      393     267    0.91       393     307    1.00
---     5      393     438    0.73       393     424    0.88
---     6      393     470    0.60       393     464    0.67
---     7      393     479    0.48       393     475    0.47
---     9      393     479    0.20       393     479    0.21
---    11      393     479    0.00       393     479    0.08
---
--- Mean deviation 2.5%, worst single frame 15%, which is inside the noise of
--- measuring a compressed 24fps capture. tests/reveal holds this table.
---
--- So the plate reads as a bar that snaps wide, opens down, and burns off. The
--- object itself is hidden for the first half of that and fades up under the
--- dissolve, which is what makes it feel like the plate became the panel rather
--- than sat in front of it. Three details carry it, and all three came out of
--- the frame table rather than out of taste:
---
---   it starts already wide and already open, never from a dot
---   it is only about 60% white when it appears, and reaches full as it lands
---   the burn starts as the height starts, so the panel is showing through
---   before the plate has finished moving
---
--- Object is what is being revealed; it must be a GuiObject with a size worth
--- standing in for. Returns a handle you can Cancel.
function Reveal.Plate(Object, Options)
	Options = Options or {}

	--- Loose, not the immediate parent: a plate dropped into a laid out frame
	--- becomes another item in the column instead of a shape over it, which is
	--- what stopped a row ever revealing itself.
	local Parent = Options.Parent or Util.Loose(Object)

	if not Parent then
		return { Cancel = function() end }
	end

	--- Nothing to measure yet, and the caller can wait: run it when there is.
	if Options.Now ~= true and not Options.Rect
		and (Object.AbsoluteSize.X < 2 or Object.AbsoluteSize.Y < 2) then
		local Handle = {}
		local Give = Ready(Object, function()
			local Run = Reveal.Plate(Object, Util.Merge(Options, { Now = true }))

			Handle.Face = Run.Face
			Handle.Cancel = Run.Cancel
		end)

		Handle.Cancel = Give

		return Handle
	end

	local X, Y, Width, Height = Rect(Object, Parent)

	--- A caller that already knows the rectangle can say so, which is the only
	--- way to reveal something on the frame it was built: a thing has no
	--- AbsoluteSize until Roblox has laid it out.
	if Options.Rect then
		X, Y, Width, Height = Options.Rect[1], Options.Rect[2], Options.Rect[3], Options.Rect[4]
	end

	--- Nothing has been laid out yet. Revealing a zero sized rectangle would
	--- draw a dot and dissolve it, which is worse than not trying.
	if Width < 2 or Height < 2 then
		return { Cancel = function() end }
	end

	local Seed = Options.Seed or 0.56
	local Open = Options.Open or 0.31

	local Face = Plate(Parent, {
		Name      = "Reveal",
		Color     = Options.Color,
		Radius    = Options.Radius,
		ZIndex    = Options.ZIndex or (Object.ZIndex + 40),
	})

	local MiddleX, MiddleY = X + Width / 2, Y + Height / 2

	--- The plate can come from somewhere. In the reference the seed bar starts
	--- a few dozen pixels off the panel's centre and drifts onto it while it
	--- grows, which is what makes it read as having come from the thing that
	--- was clicked rather than having been there all along.
	---
	--- The drift is deliberately small and capped. A plate that flies in from
	--- across the screen is a different effect, and a worse one: it draws the
	--- eye away from where the panel is about to be.
	local FromX, FromY = MiddleX, MiddleY

	if Options.From then
		local Source = Options.From
		local PointX, PointY = nil, nil

		--- Either a GuiObject to come from, or a plain point in the parent's
		--- own pixels. Read a component at a time rather than with vector
		--- arithmetic, so this works wherever the library is being run.
		if Source.AbsolutePosition then
			local Origin = Parent.AbsolutePosition
			local At = Source.AbsolutePosition
			local Span = Source.AbsoluteSize
			local PadX, PadY = Inset(Parent)

			PointX = At.X + Span.X / 2 - Origin.X - PadX
			PointY = At.Y + Span.Y / 2 - Origin.Y - PadY
		elseif Source.X and Source.Y then
			PointX, PointY = Source.X, Source.Y
		end

		if PointX then
			local AwayX = PointX - MiddleX
			local AwayY = PointY - MiddleY
			local Away = math.sqrt(AwayX * AwayX + AwayY * AwayY)
			local Cap = Options.Drift or 48

			if Away > 1 then
				local Take = math.min(Away, Cap) / Away

				FromX = MiddleX + AwayX * Take
				FromY = MiddleY + AwayY * Take
			end
		end
	end

	Face.Position = UDim2.new(0, FromX, 0, FromY)
	Face.Size = UDim2.new(0, Width * Seed, 0, Height * Open)

	--- The plate is not fully white on the frame it appears — it comes in at
	--- about 60% and reaches full as the width finishes. Starting it opaque
	--- makes the whole gesture read as a flash rather than as something being
	--- drawn.
	Face.BackgroundTransparency = Options.Ghosted or 0.4

	--- Hidden rather than transparent: a CanvasGroup fades as one, anything
	--- else has to be taken down to nothing and brought back.
	local Fade = Options.Fade
	local Resting = nil

	if Fade ~= false then
		if Object:IsA("CanvasGroup") then
			--- To is what it should end up at, which is not always what it is
			--- now: a window is revealed from closed, and closed means already
			--- transparent, so reading the current value would fade it back to
			--- nothing.
			Resting = Options.To or (Object.GroupTransparency < 1 and Object.GroupTransparency) or 0
			Object.GroupTransparency = 1
		else
			Resting = Motion.Resting(Object)

			for _, Mark in Resting do
				for Property in Mark.Bits do
					Mark.Object[Property] = 1
				end
			end
		end
	end

	local Wide = Options.Wide or "plate"
	local Tall = Options.Tall or "open"
	local Burn = Options.Burn or "burn"

	local Cancelled = false

	local function Stop()
		Cancelled = true

		Motion.Halt(Face)
		Face:Destroy()
	end

	--- Width first, then height once the width is nearly there. The overlap is
	--- deliberate: waiting for the width to settle makes it read as two moves,
	--- and starting both together makes it read as a box scaling up.
	Tween(Face, {
		Size = UDim2.new(0, Width, 0, Height * Open),
		Position = UDim2.new(0, MiddleX, 0, MiddleY),
		BackgroundTransparency = 0,
	}, Wide)

	task.delay(MotionTime(Wide) * (Options.OpenAt or 1.1), function()
		if Cancelled or not Face.Parent then
			return
		end

		Tween(Face, { Size = UDim2.new(0, Width, 0, Height) }, Tall)

		--- The dissolve starts while the height is still opening, so the panel
		--- is already showing through by the time the plate finishes moving.
		task.delay(MotionTime(Tall) * (Options.BurnAt or 0), function()
			if Cancelled or not Face.Parent then
				return
			end

			Tween(Face, { BackgroundTransparency = 1 }, Burn)

			if Fade ~= false then
				if Object:IsA("CanvasGroup") then
					Tween(Object, { GroupTransparency = Resting }, Burn)
				else
					for _, Mark in Resting do
						Tween(Mark.Object, Mark.Bits, Burn)
					end
				end
			end

			task.delay(MotionTime(Burn) * 1.2, function()
				if not Cancelled and Face.Parent then
					Face:Destroy()
				end

				if Options.Done then
					task.spawn(Options.Done)
				end
			end)
		end)
	end)

	return { Cancel = Stop, Face = Face }
end

--- The plate coming back for it.
---
--- The mirror of Plate: the white comes up over the thing, the thing goes out
--- underneath it, and then the plate shuts — height back down to a bar, width
--- to nothing. A panel that arrives as a plate and then simply vanishes when
--- you press the close button feels like two different interfaces; this is the
--- other half of the gesture.
function Reveal.Cover(Object, Options)
	Options = Options or {}

	local Parent = Options.Parent or Util.Loose(Object)

	if not Parent then
		if Options.Done then
			task.spawn(Options.Done)
		end

		return { Cancel = function() end }
	end

	local X, Y, Width, Height = Rect(Object, Parent)

	if Options.Rect then
		X, Y, Width, Height = Options.Rect[1], Options.Rect[2], Options.Rect[3], Options.Rect[4]
	end

	if Width < 2 or Height < 2 then
		if Options.Done then
			task.spawn(Options.Done)
		end

		return { Cancel = function() end }
	end

	local Seed = Options.Seed or 0.56
	local Open = Options.Open or 0.31

	local Face = Plate(Parent, {
		Name         = "Covering",
		Color        = Options.Color,
		Transparency = 1,
		Radius       = Options.Radius,
		ZIndex       = Options.ZIndex or (Object.ZIndex + 40),
	})

	Face.Position = UDim2.new(0, X + Width / 2, 0, Y + Height / 2)
	Face.Size = UDim2.new(0, Width, 0, Height)

	local Burn = Options.Burn or "plate"
	local Tall = Options.Tall or "open"
	local Wide = Options.Wide or "close"

	local Cancelled = false

	local function Stop()
		Cancelled = true

		Motion.Halt(Face)
		Face:Destroy()
	end

	--- White comes up fast, and whatever is underneath goes out with it.
	Tween(Face, { BackgroundTransparency = 0 }, Burn)

	if Options.Fade ~= false then
		if Object:IsA("CanvasGroup") then
			Tween(Object, { GroupTransparency = 1 }, Burn)
		else
			Motion.Fade(Object, 1, Burn)
		end
	end

	task.delay(MotionTime(Burn) * 1.1, function()
		if Cancelled or not Face.Parent then
			return
		end

		--- Then it shuts: down to a bar, then away to nothing.
		Tween(Face, { Size = UDim2.new(0, Width, 0, Height * Open) }, Tall)

		task.delay(MotionTime(Tall) * 0.8, function()
			if Cancelled or not Face.Parent then
				return
			end

			Tween(Face, { Size = UDim2.new(0, Width * Seed * 0.2, 0, Height * Open) }, Wide)
			Tween(Face, { BackgroundTransparency = 1 }, Wide)

			task.delay(MotionTime(Wide) * 1.1, function()
				if Face.Parent then
					Face:Destroy()
				end

				if Options.Done then
					task.spawn(Options.Done)
				end
			end)
		end)
	end)

	return { Cancel = Stop, Face = Face }
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The follow ghost
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- A white plate that chases something, and is only visible while it is behind.
---
--- This is the afterimage. The plate springs toward the object's rectangle on a
--- softer spring than the object itself uses, so a move leaves it trailing; its
--- transparency is driven by how far behind it is, so at rest it is not there at
--- all and mid move it is a smear between where the thing was and where it is
--- going.
---
--- Stretch makes the trailing plate span from its own position to the object's
--- rather than merely lagging, which is what turns a lagging copy into a smear.
function Reveal.Follow(Object, Options)
	Options = Options or {}

	local Parent = Options.Parent or Util.Loose(Object)

	if not Parent then
		return { Destroy = function() end }
	end

	local Face = Plate(Parent, {
		Name         = Options.Name or "Ghost",
		Color        = Options.Color,
		Transparency = 1,
		Radius       = Options.Radius,
		ZIndex       = Options.ZIndex or math.max(1, Object.ZIndex - 1),
	})

	local Stiffness = Options.Stiffness or 90
	local Damping = Options.Damping or (2 * math.sqrt(Options.Stiffness or 90))
	local Reach = Options.Reach or 0.55
	local Span = Options.Span or 44
	local Stretch = Options.Stretch ~= false

	local AtX, AtY = nil, nil
	local Handle = { Face = Face }

	--- The ghost costs a frame connection only while it has somewhere to be.
	--- Once it has caught up it lets go of Heartbeat, and the object's own
	--- geometry changing is what wakes it again — so a tab bar nobody is
	--- touching is not paying for a chase that is not happening.
	local Connection = nil
	local Watchers = {}

	local function Step(Delta)
		if not Object.Parent or not Face.Parent then
			return
		end

		local X, Y, Width, Height = Rect(Object, Parent)
		local MiddleX, MiddleY = X + Width / 2, Y + Height / 2

		if AtX == nil then
			AtX, AtY = MiddleX, MiddleY
		end

		--- A plain exponential chase rather than a spring: the ghost must never
		--- overshoot the thing it is trailing, or it arrives ahead of it.
		local Step = 1 - math.exp(-Stiffness * math.min(Delta, 1 / 20) / Damping * 2)

		AtX += (MiddleX - AtX) * Step
		AtY += (MiddleY - AtY) * Step

		local AwayX, AwayY = MiddleX - AtX, MiddleY - AtY
		local Away = math.sqrt(AwayX * AwayX + AwayY * AwayY)

		--- Behind by nothing means invisible. Behind by Span pixels or more
		--- means as visible as it is ever allowed to get.
		local Strength = Clamp(Away / Span, 0, 1) * Reach

		Face.BackgroundTransparency = 1 - Strength

		if Strength <= 0.002 then
			return
		end

		if Stretch then
			--- The plate covers both where the thing is and where the ghost has
			--- got to, so the gap between them is filled rather than skipped.
			local Left = math.min(AtX - Width / 2, MiddleX - Width / 2)
			local Right = math.max(AtX + Width / 2, MiddleX + Width / 2)
			local Top = math.min(AtY - Height / 2, MiddleY - Height / 2)
			local Bottom = math.max(AtY + Height / 2, MiddleY + Height / 2)

			Face.Position = UDim2.new(0, (Left + Right) / 2, 0, (Top + Bottom) / 2)
			Face.Size = UDim2.new(0, Right - Left, 0, Bottom - Top)
		else
			Face.Position = UDim2.new(0, AtX, 0, AtY)
			Face.Size = UDim2.new(0, Width, 0, Height)
		end
	end

	local function Sleep()
		if Connection then
			Connection:Disconnect()
			Connection = nil
		end
	end

	local function Wake()
		if not Connection and Face.Parent then
			Connection = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(Delta)
				Step(Delta)

				if Face.BackgroundTransparency > 0.998 then
					Sleep()
				end
			end)
		end
	end

	Handle.Wake = Wake

	for _, Property in { "AbsolutePosition", "AbsoluteSize" } do
		table.insert(Watchers, Object:GetPropertyChangedSignal(Property):Connect(Wake))
	end

	function Handle:Destroy()
		Sleep()

		for _, Watcher in Watchers do
			Watcher:Disconnect()
		end

		table.clear(Watchers)
		Face:Destroy()
	end

	--- Puts the ghost exactly where the object is, so a jump that should not
	--- smear does not.
	function Handle:Settle()
		local X, Y, Width, Height = Rect(Object, Parent)

		AtX, AtY = X + Width / 2, Y + Height / 2
		Face.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		Sleep()

		return Handle
	end

	return Handle
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- One shot afterimages
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- A single white copy of where something was, left behind to fade.
---
--- Unlike Follow, this does not track anything: it is stamped at a moment and
--- then it dies. Stamp one per frame while something moves and you have a trail
--- you can control precisely; stamp one when something is removed and it reads
--- as the thing leaving a hole behind it.
function Reveal.Ghost(Object, Options)
	Options = Options or {}

	local Parent = Options.Parent or Util.Loose(Object)

	if not Parent then
		return nil
	end

	local X, Y, Width, Height = Rect(Object, Parent)

	if Width < 1 or Height < 1 then
		return nil
	end

	local Face = Plate(Parent, {
		Name         = "Afterimage",
		Color        = Options.Color,
		Transparency = Options.Transparency or 0.55,
		Radius       = Options.Radius,
		ZIndex       = Options.ZIndex or math.max(1, Object.ZIndex - 1),
	})

	Face.Position = UDim2.new(0, X + Width / 2, 0, Y + Height / 2)
	Face.Size = UDim2.new(0, Width, 0, Height)

	local Role = Options.Role or "smear"

	Tween(Face, {
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		Size = UDim2.new(0, Width * (Options.Spread or 1), 0, Height * (Options.Spread or 1)),
	}, Role)

	task.delay(MotionTime(Role) * 1.3, function()
		if Face.Parent then
			Face:Destroy()
		end
	end)

	return Face
end

--- A trail of them. Stamps a ghost every Every seconds for as long as the
--- object keeps moving, and stops on its own once it settles.
function Reveal.Trail(Object, Options)
	Options = Options or {}

	local Parent = Options.Parent or Util.Loose(Object)
	local Every = Options.Every or 1 / 30
	local Least = Options.Least or 3

	local Since = 0
	local LastX, LastY = nil, nil

	local Connection = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(Delta)
		if not Object.Parent then
			return
		end

		local Point = Object.AbsolutePosition

		if LastX then
			local Moved = math.abs(Point.X - LastX) + math.abs(Point.Y - LastY)

			Since += Delta

			if Moved > Least and Since >= Every then
				Since = 0
				Reveal.Ghost(Object, {
					Parent       = Parent,
					Color        = Options.Color,
					Transparency = Options.Transparency,
					Radius       = Options.Radius,
					Role         = Options.Role,
					Spread       = Options.Spread,
				})
			end
		end

		LastX, LastY = Point.X, Point.Y
	end)

	return {
		Destroy = function()
			Connection:Disconnect()
		end,
	}
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Wipes
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- A white bar that sweeps across something and leaves it behind, uncovered.
---
--- The bar is the width of the object and travels its length; the object is
--- clipped to the part the bar has already passed, so the content is not there
--- until the white has been over it.
function Reveal.Wipe(Object, Options)
	Options = Options or {}

	local Parent = Options.Parent or Util.Loose(Object)

	if not Parent then
		return { Cancel = function() end }
	end

	if Options.Now ~= true and (Object.AbsoluteSize.X < 2 or Object.AbsoluteSize.Y < 2) then
		local Handle = {}
		local Give = Ready(Object, function()
			local Run = Reveal.Wipe(Object, Util.Merge(Options, { Now = true }))

			Handle.Face = Run.Face
			Handle.Cancel = Run.Cancel
		end)

		Handle.Cancel = Give

		return Handle
	end

	local X, Y, Width, Height = Rect(Object, Parent)

	if Width < 2 or Height < 2 then
		return { Cancel = function() end }
	end

	local Down = Options.Axis == "Y"
	local Thickness = Options.Thickness or (Down and math.max(2, Height * 0.18) or math.max(2, Width * 0.12))

	local Bar = Plate(Parent, {
		Name   = "Wipe",
		Color  = Options.Color,
		ZIndex = Options.ZIndex or (Object.ZIndex + 40),
	})

	Bar.Size = Down and UDim2.new(0, Width, 0, Thickness) or UDim2.new(0, Thickness, 0, Height)
	Bar.Position = Down
		and UDim2.new(0, X + Width / 2, 0, Y)
		or UDim2.new(0, X, 0, Y + Height / 2)

	local Resting = Motion.Resting(Object)

	for _, Mark in Resting do
		for Property in Mark.Bits do
			Mark.Object[Property] = 1
		end
	end

	local Role = Options.Role or "sweep"
	local Landed = false

	Tween(Bar, {
		Position = Down
			and UDim2.new(0, X + Width / 2, 0, Y + Height)
			or UDim2.new(0, X + Width, 0, Y + Height / 2),
	}, Role)

	--- The content comes up behind the bar rather than after it, so the bar is
	--- always ahead of what it has revealed.
	task.delay(MotionTime(Role) * 0.35, function()
		if Landed then
			return
		end

		for _, Mark in Resting do
			if Mark.Object.Parent then
				Tween(Mark.Object, Mark.Bits, "enter")
			end
		end
	end)

	task.delay(MotionTime(Role), function()
		if not Landed and Bar.Parent then
			Tween(Bar, { BackgroundTransparency = 1 }, "burn")

			task.delay(MotionTime("burn") * 1.2, function()
				if Bar.Parent then
					Bar:Destroy()
				end
			end)
		end
	end)

	return {
		Face = Bar,
		Cancel = function()
			Landed = true
			Motion.Halt(Bar)
			Bar:Destroy()

			for _, Mark in Resting do
				if Mark.Object.Parent then
					for Property, Value in Mark.Bits do
						Mark.Object[Property] = Value
					end
				end
			end
		end,
	}
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Closing
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- A white bar that contracts to nothing about its own centre, handing over to
--- whatever was underneath it.
---
--- The opposite gesture to a plate: a plate arrives by growing, this leaves by
--- closing. It is what covers a cut in the reference — the screen goes black in
--- a single frame and a bar over the label's position closes away, so the label
--- is uncovered rather than faded up.
---
--- Measured at 24fps over a 215 px bar: 215, 191, 159, 129, 81, 61, 47, 35, 18,
--- 13, 9. A critically damped spring at a stiffness of 144 lands within a pixel
--- or two of every one of those.
function Reveal.Close(Object, Options)
	Options = Options or {}

	local Parent = Options.Parent or (Object and Util.Loose(Object))

	if not Parent then
		return { Cancel = function() end }
	end

	local X, Y, Width, Height = 0, 0, 0, 0

	if Options.Rect then
		X, Y, Width, Height = Options.Rect[1], Options.Rect[2], Options.Rect[3], Options.Rect[4]
	elseif Object then
		X, Y, Width, Height = Rect(Object, Parent)
	end

	if Width < 2 or Height < 1 then
		return { Cancel = function() end }
	end

	--- Wider than what it covers, because the bar in the reference overhangs
	--- the label it hands over to rather than matching it.
	local Over = Options.Over or 1.1

	local Face = Plate(Parent, {
		Name   = "Closing",
		Color  = Options.Color,
		Radius = Options.Radius,
		ZIndex = Options.ZIndex or ((Object and Object.ZIndex or 1) + 40),
	})

	Face.Position = UDim2.new(0, X + Width / 2, 0, Y + Height / 2)
	Face.Size = UDim2.new(0, Width * Over, 0, Height)

	local Role = Options.Role or "close"
	local Gone = false

	--- Height held, width taken to nothing: it closes like a shutter rather
	--- than shrinking like a box.
	Tween(Face, { Size = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, Height) }, Role)

	task.delay(MotionTime(Role) * 1.2, function()
		if not Gone and Face.Parent then
			Face:Destroy()
		end

		if Options.Done then
			task.spawn(Options.Done)
		end
	end)

	return {
		Face = Face,
		Cancel = function()
			Gone = true
			Motion.Halt(Face)
			Face:Destroy()
		end,
	}
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Screen level
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- A white flash over everything.
---
--- Measured off the reference at 30fps: it snaps to full white in one frame,
--- HOLDS there for five (0.17 s), and only then decays over about seven more.
--- The hold is the part that is easy to leave out and the part that makes it
--- read as a cut being covered rather than as a light being flicked — without
--- it the flash is a blink, and a blink cannot hide a scene change behind it.
function Reveal.Flash(Options)
	Options = Options or {}

	local Screen = require(script.Parent.Screen)

	local Face = New("Frame", {
		Name                   = "Flash",
		Parent                 = Options.Parent or Screen.Get(),
		BackgroundColor3       = Options.Color or Theme.White,
		BackgroundTransparency = 1 - (Options.Peak or 0.9),
		BorderSizePixel        = 0,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0),
		ZIndex                 = Options.ZIndex or 4000,
		Active                 = false,
		Selectable             = false,
	})

	--- Every pixel, top bar included. A flash that misses a strip at the bottom
	--- of the screen is not a flash.
	Screen.Cover(Face)

	local Role = Options.Role or "burn"
	local Hold = Options.Hold or 0

	local function Decay()
		if not Face.Parent then
			return
		end

		Tween(Face, { BackgroundTransparency = 1 }, Role)

		task.delay(MotionTime(Role) * 1.4, function()
			if Face.Parent then
				Face:Destroy()
			end
		end)
	end

	--- Anything covered by the flash happens at the top of the hold, while the
	--- screen is solid, which is the whole reason to hold at all.
	if Hold > 0 then
		task.delay(Hold, function()
			if Options.Covered then
				task.spawn(Options.Covered)
			end

			Decay()
		end)
	else
		if Options.Covered then
			task.spawn(Options.Covered)
		end

		Decay()
	end

	return Face
end

return Reveal
Screen:
--!nonstrict
--- Screen.luau — the one ScreenGui everything lands in, plus the modal count.
---
--- The modal count is global on purpose: a prompt has to be able to silence
--- the scroll wheel and the toggle keys of windows it knows nothing about.

local Players    = game:GetService("Players")
local GuiService = game:GetService("GuiService")

local Util = require(script.Parent.Util)

local New = Util.New

local Screen = {}

local LocalPlayer = Players.LocalPlayer
local Host = nil

--- Rebuilds itself if something destroys the GUI out from under us, which is
--- what Kuik.Reset does.
function Screen.Get()
	if Host and Host.Parent then
		return Host
	end

	local Parent = LocalPlayer and LocalPlayer:FindFirstChildOfClass("PlayerGui")

	Host = New("ScreenGui", {
		Name             = "Kuik",
		Parent           = Parent,
		ResetOnSpawn     = false,
		IgnoreGuiInset   = true,
		ZIndexBehavior   = Enum.ZIndexBehavior.Sibling,
		DisplayOrder     = 50,
	})

	return Host
end

--- How much of the top of the screen the platform has taken.
---
--- The one ScreenGui ignores the inset on purpose, so a full bleed thing — a
--- vignette, a flash, a loading sheet — really does cover the screen. The cost
--- is that anything measured as a fraction from the top can land underneath the
--- top bar, so anything that has to stay clear of it adds this back.
function Screen.Inset()
	local Ok, Top = pcall(function()
		return GuiService:GetGuiInset()
	end)

	return Ok and Top and Top.Y or 0
end

--- A y position given as a fraction of what the player can actually see,
--- returned as offset pixels from the top of the inset ignoring layer.
---
--- Measured rather than assumed. With IgnoreGuiInset, Roblox moves the layer up
--- by the inset and leaves its size alone: against a 1532 x 619 viewport with a
--- 58 px bar, the layer reports position (0, -58) and size 1532 x 619. So the
--- visible window is the layer's own height, starting one inset down from the
--- layer's top.
function Screen.Safe(Fraction, Height)
	local Top = Screen.Inset()
	local Tall = Height or math.max(0, Screen.Get().AbsoluteSize.Y)

	return Top + Tall * (Fraction or 0)
end

--- Makes something cover the whole window, top bar included.
---
--- The same measurement is why this exists: a child of the layer sized
--- (1, 0, 1, 0) covers the bar at the top and leaves exactly one inset of the
--- screen UNCOVERED at the bottom. Everything full bleed — a flash, a vignette,
--- a backdrop, a loading sheet — has to be a bar taller than it looks.
function Screen.Cover(Object)
	local Top = Screen.Inset()

	Object.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)
	Object.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, Top)

	return Object
end

function Screen.Destroy()
	if Host then
		Host:Destroy()
		Host = nil
	end
end

local Modals = 0
local Watchers = {}

--- True while anything modal is up. Input handlers check this before acting so
--- the world behind a prompt stays inert.
function Screen.Blocked()
	return Modals > 0
end

function Screen.Depth()
	return Modals
end

function Screen.Enter()
	Modals += 1

	for _, Handler in Watchers do
		task.spawn(Handler, Modals)
	end
end

function Screen.Exit()
	Modals = math.max(0, Modals - 1)

	for _, Handler in Watchers do
		task.spawn(Handler, Modals)
	end
end

--- Lets a control react to the world going modal, rather than only poll it.
function Screen.OnModal(Handler)
	table.insert(Watchers, Handler)

	return function()
		local At = table.find(Watchers, Handler)

		if At then
			table.remove(Watchers, At)
		end
	end
end

Screen.Player = LocalPlayer

return Screen
Scroll:
--!nonstrict
--- Scroll.luau — smooth wheel scrolling and the edge gleams that tell you
--- there is more.
---
--- Roblox's own wheel handling snaps. The fix is to turn ScrollingEnabled off
--- on desktop and drive CanvasPosition with a spring instead, which also means
--- a scroll can be retargeted mid flight by another wheel tick.

local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

local Palette = require(script.Parent.Theme)
local Util    = require(script.Parent.Util)
local Motion  = require(script.Parent.Motion)
local Screen  = require(script.Parent.Screen)

local Theme = Palette.Tokens

local New   = Util.New
local Clamp = Util.Clamp

local Tween      = Motion.Tween
local MotionTime = Motion.MotionTime

local Scroll = {}

--- A soft light at each end of a scroller, fading off along its own edges so
--- it reads as a gradient rather than a stripe. Built from a CanvasGroup with
--- a cross axis gradient wrapping a frame with a main axis one, because a
--- UIGradient only has the one axis.
local function Gleam(Frame, Vertical, Depth, Options)
	local Parent = Util.Loose(Frame)

	if not Parent then
		return function() end
	end

	Options = Options or {}
	Depth = Depth or 22

	local Base = Options.Strength or 0.86
	local Colour = Options.Color or Theme.White

	local function Edge(Head)
		local Group = New("CanvasGroup", {
			Name                   = Head and "GleamHead" or "GleamTail",
			Parent                 = Parent,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			GroupTransparency      = 1,
			BorderSizePixel        = 0,
			ZIndex                 = 30,
			Active                 = false,
		}, {
			New("UIGradient", {
				Rotation = Vertical and 0 or 90,
				Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
					NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 1),
					NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.16, 0),
					NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.84, 0),
					NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1),
				}),
			}),
		})

		New("Frame", {
			Name                   = "Light",
			Parent                 = Group,
			BackgroundColor3       = Colour,
			BackgroundTransparency = Base,
			BorderSizePixel        = 0,
			Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0),
			Active                 = false,
		}, {
			New("UIGradient", {
				Rotation = Vertical and 90 or 0,
				Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
					NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, Head and 0 or 1),
					NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, Head and 1 or 0),
				}),
			}),
		})

		return Group
	end

	local Head, Tail = Edge(true), Edge(false)

	--- The gleams are not children of the scroller, so they never take part in
	--- its layout or get clipped by it — which means tracking its geometry by
	--- hand. Measured in absolutes rather than copied from Position and Size,
	--- because the host they hang off is no longer always the scroller's own
	--- parent: it is the first ancestor that is not arranging its children.
	local function Layout()
		local Origin = Parent.AbsolutePosition
		local At = Frame.AbsolutePosition
		local Size = Frame.AbsoluteSize

		if Size.X <= 0 or Size.Y <= 0 then
			return
		end

		local X, Y = At.X - Origin.X, At.Y - Origin.Y

		if Vertical then
			Head.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0, 0)
			Head.Position = UDim2.new(0, X, 0, Y)
			Head.Size = UDim2.new(0, Size.X, 0, Depth)

			Tail.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0, 1)
			Tail.Position = UDim2.new(0, X, 0, Y + Size.Y)
			Tail.Size = UDim2.new(0, Size.X, 0, Depth)
		else
			Head.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0, 0)
			Head.Position = UDim2.new(0, X, 0, Y)
			Head.Size = UDim2.new(0, Depth, 0, Size.Y)

			Tail.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0)
			Tail.Position = UDim2.new(0, X + Size.X, 0, Y)
			Tail.Size = UDim2.new(0, Depth, 0, Size.Y)
		end
	end

	local Motion_ = 0
	local Before, After = false, false

	local function Update()
		local Span = Vertical
			and Frame.AbsoluteCanvasSize.Y - Frame.AbsoluteSize.Y
			or Frame.AbsoluteCanvasSize.X - Frame.AbsoluteSize.X

		local At = Vertical and Frame.CanvasPosition.Y or Frame.CanvasPosition.X

		Before = Span > 2 and At > 2
		After = Span > 2 and (Span - At) > 2

		Tween(Head, { GroupTransparency = Before and Motion_ or 1 }, "fade")
		Tween(Tail, { GroupTransparency = After and Motion_ or 1 }, "fade")
	end

	--- While the wheel is moving the gleams dim, then settle back once it
	--- stops. It reads as the light reacting to the motion.
	local Settle = 0

	local function Nudge()
		Motion_ = 0.55
		Settle += 1

		local Mine = Settle

		Tween(Head, { GroupTransparency = Before and Motion_ or 1 }, "hover")
		Tween(Tail, { GroupTransparency = After and Motion_ or 1 }, "hover")

		task.delay(MotionTime("scroll") * 0.9, function()
			if Settle == Mine then
				Motion_ = 0
				Update()
			end
		end)
	end

	local Connections = {
		Frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsolutePosition"):Connect(Layout),
		Frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"):Connect(Layout),
		Parent:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsolutePosition"):Connect(Layout),
		Frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CanvasPosition"):Connect(Update),
		Frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteCanvasSize"):Connect(Update),
		Frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"):Connect(Update),
	}

	Layout()
	task.defer(Update)

	return function()
		for _, Connection in Connections do
			Connection:Disconnect()
		end

		Head:Destroy()
		Tail:Destroy()
	end, Nudge
end

--- Gleams on the inside edges of something that can be moved further than it
--- shows: the four faces of a panned image, the two ends of a carousel. Unlike
--- the scroller gleams above these are children of the frame itself, because
--- the frame clips and the light should be clipped with it.
---
--- Each edge is lit in proportion to how far there is left to go that way, so
--- the light is a readout of the room remaining rather than a decoration.
local function Edges(Frame, Options)
	Options = Options or {}

	local Depth = Options.Depth or 26
	local Base = Options.Strength or 0.72
	local Colour = Options.Color or Theme.White

	local Sides = {}

	local function Edge(Name, Anchor, Position, Size, Rotation)
		local Group = New("CanvasGroup", {
			Name                   = Name,
			Parent                 = Frame,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			GroupTransparency      = 1,
			BorderSizePixel        = 0,
			AnchorPoint            = Anchor,
			Position               = Position,
			Size                   = Size,
			ZIndex                 = Options.ZIndex or 20,
			Active                 = false,
		})

		New("Frame", {
			Name                   = "Light",
			Parent                 = Group,
			BackgroundColor3       = Colour,
			BackgroundTransparency = Base,
			BorderSizePixel        = 0,
			Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0),
			Active                 = false,
		}, {
			New("UIGradient", {
				Rotation = Rotation,
				Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
					NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0),
					NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1),
				}),
			}),
		})

		Sides[Name] = Group

		return Group
	end

	--- Rotation points each gradient away from its own edge, so the light is
	--- strongest against the frame and gone by the time it reaches the middle.
	Edge("Left", Vector2.new(0, 0), UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0), UDim2.new(0, Depth, 1, 0), 0)
	Edge("Right", Vector2.new(1, 0), UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0), UDim2.new(0, Depth, 1, 0), 180)
	Edge("Top", Vector2.new(0, 0), UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0), UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, Depth), 90)
	Edge("Bottom", Vector2.new(0, 1), UDim2.new(0, 0, 1, 0), UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, Depth), 270)

	local Handle = { Sides = Sides }

	--- Room is a 0..1 per side. Anything past a tenth of the depth is treated
	--- as fully lit, so a small amount of travel still reads clearly.
	function Handle:Set(Room, Role)
		for Name, Group in Sides do
			local Amount = math.clamp((Room[Name] or 0) * 8, 0, 1)

			Tween(Group, { GroupTransparency = 1 - Amount }, Role or "fade")
		end

		return Handle
	end

	function Handle:Destroy()
		for _, Group in Sides do
			Group:Destroy()
		end

		table.clear(Sides)
	end

	return Handle
end

--- Which scroller the pointer is over. Module wide so the innermost one wins:
--- scrolling a dropdown should not also scroll the page behind it.
local Hovered = nil

local function SmoothScroll(Frame, Axis, Options)
	local Handle = { Frame = Frame, Enabled = true }
	local Vertical = Axis ~= "X"

	if not (Options and Options.Gleam == false) then
		Handle.StopGleam, Handle.Nudge = Gleam(Frame, Vertical,
			Options and Options.Depth, Options)
	end

	--- Touch and gamepad keep Roblox's own scrolling: it is already right for
	--- them, and taking it over would break momentum.
	if not UserInputService.MouseEnabled then
		function Handle:SetEnabled() end
		function Handle:Sync() end

		function Handle:To(Position)
			Frame.CanvasPosition = Position
		end

		function Handle:Top()
			Frame.CanvasPosition = Vector2.zero
		end

		function Handle:Span()
			return math.max(0, Vertical
				and Frame.AbsoluteCanvasSize.Y - Frame.AbsoluteSize.Y
				or Frame.AbsoluteCanvasSize.X - Frame.AbsoluteSize.X)
		end

		function Handle:Destroy()
			if Handle.StopGleam then
				Handle.StopGleam()
			end
		end

		return Handle
	end

	Frame.ScrollingEnabled = false

	local Target = Frame.CanvasPosition
	local Connections = {}

	--- Whether the viewer has ever scrolled this frame themselves. Until they
	--- have, a canvas that grows must not drag the view: content is still
	--- being built, and a window that opens already scrolled to the bottom is
	--- the single most confusing thing a UI can do.
	local Touched = false

	function Handle:SetEnabled(Value)
		Handle.Enabled = Value
	end

	function Handle:To(Position, Role)
		Touched = true
		Target = Position
		Tween(Frame, { CanvasPosition = Target }, Role or "scroll")
	end

	function Handle:Sync()
		Target = Frame.CanvasPosition
	end

	--- Back to the start, and forget that anyone had scrolled.
	function Handle:Top()
		Touched = false
		Target = Vector2.zero
		Frame.CanvasPosition = Vector2.zero
		Motion.Halt(Frame, "CanvasPosition")
	end

	function Handle:Span()
		return math.max(0, Vertical
			and Frame.AbsoluteCanvasSize.Y - Frame.AbsoluteSize.Y
			or Frame.AbsoluteCanvasSize.X - Frame.AbsoluteSize.X)
	end

	--- Content shrinking underneath a scrolled view would otherwise leave the
	--- canvas parked past its own end.
	--- Until the viewer has scrolled this frame themselves, it is pinned to the
	--- start. Content arriving, the frame being resized, the window being
	--- fitted to a viewport that was not measured yet — any of them can leave
	--- a freshly built scroller parked at the bottom of its own content, which
	--- is the single most confusing thing a panel can do. Rather than chase
	--- each cause, the invariant is enforced directly.
	local Holding = false

	local function Pin()
		if Touched or Holding then
			return
		end

		if Frame.CanvasPosition.Magnitude > 0.5 then
			Holding = true
			Target = Vector2.zero
			Frame.CanvasPosition = Vector2.zero
			Holding = false
		end
	end

	table.insert(Connections, Frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CanvasPosition"):Connect(Pin))
	table.insert(Connections, Frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"):Connect(Pin))

	table.insert(Connections, Frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteCanvasSize"):Connect(function()
		if not Touched then
			Pin()
			return
		end

		local Span = Handle:Span()

		if Vertical and Target.Y > Span then
			Handle:To(Vector2.new(0, Span))
		elseif not Vertical and Target.X > Span then
			Handle:To(Vector2.new(Span, 0))
		end
	end))

	local Driving = false
	local Token = 0

	table.insert(Connections, Frame.MouseEnter:Connect(function()
		Hovered = Frame
	end))

	table.insert(Connections, Frame.MouseLeave:Connect(function()
		if Hovered == Frame then
			Hovered = nil
		end
	end))

	table.insert(Connections, Frame.InputChanged:Connect(function(Input)
		if not Handle.Enabled or Input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.MouseWheel then
			return
		end

		--- A prompt is up: the wheel belongs to it, or to nothing.
		if Screen.Blocked() and not (Options and Options.Modal) then
			return
		end

		--- Someone nested inside us owns this tick.
		if Hovered and Hovered ~= Frame then
			return
		end

		local Span = Handle:Span()

		if Span <= 0 then
			return
		end

		Touched = true

		--- Resync from the real position when the previous scroll has settled,
		--- so a drag or a jump elsewhere does not get undone by the next tick.
		if not Driving then
			Target = Frame.CanvasPosition
		end

		local Step = Input.Position.Z * (Options and Options.Step or (Vertical and 92 or 56))

		Target = Vertical
			and Vector2.new(0, Clamp(Target.Y - Step, 0, Span))
			or Vector2.new(Clamp(Target.X - Step, 0, Span), 0)

		Driving = true
		Token += 1

		local Mine = Token

		if Handle.Nudge then
			Handle.Nudge()
		end

		Tween(Frame, { CanvasPosition = Target }, "scroll")

		task.delay(MotionTime("scroll") * 1.2, function()
			if Token == Mine then
				Driving = false
			end
		end)
	end))

	function Handle:Destroy()
		for _, Connection in Connections do
			Connection:Disconnect()
		end

		table.clear(Connections)

		if Handle.StopGleam then
			Handle.StopGleam()
		end

		if Hovered == Frame then
			Hovered = nil
		end
	end

	return Handle
end

Scroll.Gleam  = Gleam
Scroll.Edges  = Edges
Scroll.Attach = SmoothScroll

function Scroll.Hovered()
	return Hovered
end

return Scroll

--!nonstrict
--- Shared.luau — the seam that keeps the module graph acyclic.
---
--- Controls need Attach, Attach lives in Layout, and Layout is built out of
--- Controls. Rather than a require cycle, Layout writes itself in here and the
--- controls read it at call time, by which point everything is loaded.

local Shared = {}

--- Filled in by the modules that own them:
---   Shared.Attach  (Object) -> Object          Layout
---   Shared.Window  (Options) -> Window         Window
---   Shared.Tabs    (Owner, Options) -> Tabs    Layout
---   Shared.Section (Owner, ...) -> Section     Layout

return Shared

--!nonstrict
--- Theme.luau — every colour, size and motion number Kuik draws with.
---
--- The token tables are mutated in place rather than replaced, so anything
--- holding a reference to them keeps seeing the current theme. Objects painted
--- with a token are remembered in a weak registry, which is what lets
--- Kuik.SetTheme repaint a UI that is already on screen.

local Palette = {}

--- Colour tokens. Everything visible resolves to one of these, so a theme is
--- nothing more than a different set of values under the same names.
local Theme = {
	Font       = Font.fromName("Montserrat", Enum.FontWeight.Regular),
	FontMedium = Font.fromName("Montserrat", Enum.FontWeight.Medium),
	FontBold   = Font.fromName("Montserrat", Enum.FontWeight.SemiBold),
	FontMono   = Font.fromEnum(Enum.Font.Code),

	--- Ink and ground. White is what type and rules are drawn in; Black backs
	--- the chips and knobs; Scrim is the wash behind a window.
	White = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255),
	Black = Color3.fromRGB(20, 20, 20),
	Scrim = Color3.fromRGB(8, 8, 10),

	--- Type is transparency over White, not a second colour, so it stays
	--- correct over any backdrop.
	TextPrimary   = 0.00,
	TextSecondary = 0.42,
	TextTertiary  = 0.58,
	TextDisabled  = 0.72,

	RuleTransparency = 0.45,

	RowTransparency      = 0.94,
	RowHoverTransparency = 0.88,
	RowPressTransparency = 0.82,

	ChipTransparency = 0.45,

	--- Media wells: the dark plate an image or viewport sits on. Set
	--- EmbedTransparency to 1 for embeds with no plate at all.
	EmbedColor        = Color3.fromRGB(20, 20, 20),
	EmbedTransparency = 0.65,

	Danger  = Color3.fromRGB(255, 72, 72),
	Warn    = Color3.fromRGB(255, 176, 46),
	Info    = Color3.fromRGB(96, 156, 255),
	Good    = Color3.fromRGB(96, 210, 128),
	Neutral = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255),
	Accent  = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255),

	--- Named motion. Anything with a Duration is a tween; anything with a
	--- Stiffness is a spring, which is what most of the library uses.
	--- Everything the library moves, moves on a spring. A spring retargets in
	--- flight instead of restarting, so a value that changes twice in three
	--- frames bends toward the new goal rather than stuttering — which is the
	--- whole reason these are not tweens.
	---
	--- Damping is read as a ratio against the frequency: at 2 * sqrt(Stiffness)
	--- a spring is critically damped and never overshoots. Anything that moves
	--- a transparency or a colour is kept at or above critical, because an
	--- overshoot there clips at the end of the range and reads as a flicker.
	--- Anything that moves a position or a size is allowed to overshoot a
	--- little, because that is what makes it feel alive.
	Motion = {
		instant = { Duration = 0 },

		enter  = { Stiffness = 170,  Damping = 24 },
		exit   = { Stiffness = 250,  Damping = 32 },
		expand = { Stiffness = 310,  Damping = 34 },
		hint   = { Stiffness = 740,  Damping = 56 },
		item   = { Stiffness = 400,  Damping = 40 },
		list   = { Stiffness = 460,  Damping = 43 },
		drop   = { Stiffness = 170,  Damping = 19 },

		--- At or above critical: these carry transparency and colour.
		hover  = { Stiffness = 2500, Damping = 100 },
		press  = { Stiffness = 7300, Damping = 171 },
		fade   = { Stiffness = 310,  Damping = 36 },
		tint   = { Stiffness = 420,  Damping = 42 },

		--- The white layer. These four came off a frame table rather than out of
		--- the air: a plate snaps wide in about an eighth of a second, opens
		--- down in about a fifth, and burns off in about a quarter.
		plate  = { Stiffness = 5000, Damping = 142 },
		open   = { Stiffness = 1500, Damping = 78 },
		burn   = { Stiffness = 200,  Damping = 29 },
		smear  = { Stiffness = 400,  Damping = 40 },
		sweep  = { Stiffness = 294,  Damping = 34 },

		--- A white bar closing to nothing. Fitted against eleven frames of the
		--- reference and it lands within a pixel or two on every one of them.
		close  = { Stiffness = 144,  Damping = 24 },

		layout = { Stiffness = 190, Damping = 24 },
		morph  = { Stiffness = 210, Damping = 26 },
		drag   = { Stiffness = 620, Damping = 42 },
		toss   = { Stiffness = 340, Damping = 22 },
		reveal = { Stiffness = 150, Damping = 20 },
		snap   = { Stiffness = 600, Damping = 40 },
		pop    = { Stiffness = 420, Damping = 28 },
		shrink = { Stiffness = 520, Damping = 46 },

		--- Deliberately over critical: the wheel should never overshoot.
		scroll = { Stiffness = 300, Damping = 38 },
	},
}

--- Sizes. Radii live here too, which is why squaring off the whole library is
--- three numbers rather than a search across forty files.
local Metrics = {
	--- Whether a panel arrives as a white plate rather than by fading up. On,
	--- because it is the single thing that makes the library look like the house
	--- it is modelled on — but only for windows that are panels: a HUD element
	--- with no chrome opens without ceremony, and a Bare or Panel variant is
	--- therefore left alone whatever this says.
	Reveal        = true,

	--- How every overlay — menu, popover, sheet, drawer, prompt — is dressed
	--- unless it says otherwise. "Card" is a dark plate; "Rules" is the house
	--- style, two hairlines and almost no fill.
	OverlayVariant = "Card",

	WindowWidth   = 460,
	WindowHeight  = 500,
	WindowPadding = 26,

	TitleSize    = 27,
	SubtitleSize = 14,

	SectionTitleSize = 18,
	SectionDescSize  = 12,

	--- The type scale. Every size in the library is one of these names, never
	--- an offset from another one: a caption that is "RowDescSize - 3" cannot
	--- be tuned without doing arithmetic in your head at forty call sites.
	RowLabelSize = 16,
	RowDescSize  = 16,
	SubheadSize  = 14,
	BodySize     = 15,
	ValueSize    = 14,
	CaptionSize  = 13,
	TinySize     = 11,
	RowHeight    = 46,
	RowHeightTall = 62,
	RowGap       = 16,
	RowPadding   = 14,
	RowRadius    = 0,
	CardRadius   = 0,
	PillRadius   = 0,

	TabHeight  = 30,
	TabPadding = 14,
	TabGap     = 6,
	TabIcon    = 14,

	ToggleWidth  = 50,
	ToggleHeight = 25,
	KnobInset    = 3,
	CheckSize    = 18,

	SliderTrack = 3,
	SliderThumbWidth  = 4,
	SliderThumbHeight = 15,

	ChipWidth  = 52,
	ChipHeight = 23,
	ChipRadius = 5,

	--- Monospaced sizes: the small readouts the library sets numbers in.
	MonoSize      = 10,
	MonoBoldSize  = 11,
	MonoLargeSize = 12,

	--- The one oversized readout in the library: an ammo count.
	CountSize = 22,

	StrokeThickness = 1,
}

Palette.Tokens  = Theme
Palette.Metrics = Metrics

--- The properties worth repainting. Colour properties are matched by value,
--- which is reliable because theme colours are distinctive; transparency is
--- matched only against the named text and surface tokens.
local COLOUR_PROPERTIES = {
	"BackgroundColor3",
	"TextColor3",
	"ImageColor3",
	"PlaceholderColor3",
	"BorderColor3",
	"Color",
}

local ALPHA_PROPERTIES = {
	"BackgroundTransparency",
	"TextTransparency",
	"ImageTransparency",
	"Transparency",
}

local COLOUR_TOKENS = {
	"White", "Black", "Scrim", "EmbedColor",
	"Danger", "Warn", "Info", "Good", "Neutral", "Accent",
}

--- 0 is left out on purpose: it means "fully opaque" far more often than it
--- means "primary type", and repainting every opaque thing would be wrong.
local ALPHA_TOKENS = {
	"TextSecondary", "TextTertiary", "TextDisabled",
	"RuleTransparency",
	"RowTransparency", "RowHoverTransparency", "RowPressTransparency",
	"ChipTransparency",
	"EmbedTransparency",
}

--- Object -> { [Property] = Token }. Weak keys, so a destroyed instance drops
--- out of the registry on its own.
local Painted = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

--- Records anything drawn in a theme colour so SetTheme can find it again.
--- Called by Util.New for every object it builds, which is all of them.
function Palette.Track(Object, Properties)
	local Record = nil

	--- Matched by value rather than by type: equality with a known colour
