	--- token is itself the type check, and it is the only form that works
	--- headlessly, where typeof cannot be shimmed.
	for _, Property in COLOUR_PROPERTIES do
		local Value = Properties[Property]

		if Value ~= nil then
			for _, Token in COLOUR_TOKENS do
				if Theme[Token] == Value then
					Record = Record or {}
					Record[Property] = Token
					break
				end
			end
		end
	end

	for _, Property in ALPHA_PROPERTIES do
		local Value = Properties[Property]

		if type(Value) == "number" then
			for _, Token in ALPHA_TOKENS do
				if Theme[Token] == Value then
					Record = Record or {}
					Record[Property] = Token
					break
				end
			end
		end
	end

	if Record then
		Painted[Object] = Record
	end
end

--- Paints an object with tokens by name, for the places that set a colour
--- after construction and still want it to follow the theme.
function Palette.Paint(Object, Map)
	local Record = Painted[Object] or {}

	for Property, Token in Map do
		Record[Property] = Token
		Object[Property] = Theme[Token]
	end

	Painted[Object] = Record
end

--- Stops an object following the theme, for a colour the caller owns.
function Palette.Release(Object)
	Painted[Object] = nil
end

--- The presets. A theme is a sparse overlay: anything it leaves out keeps the
--- default, so a two-line theme is a perfectly good theme.
Palette.Themes = {
	Remorse = {},

	Redliner = {
		Accent = Color3.fromRGB(255, 62, 62),
		Info   = Color3.fromRGB(255, 62, 62),
		Scrim  = Color3.fromRGB(10, 6, 6),
		Black  = Color3.fromRGB(24, 16, 16),
	},

	Ember = {
		Accent = Color3.fromRGB(255, 138, 46),
		Info   = Color3.fromRGB(255, 138, 46),
		Scrim  = Color3.fromRGB(14, 9, 5),
		Black  = Color3.fromRGB(28, 20, 14),
	},

	Terminal = {
		White  = Color3.fromRGB(198, 255, 208),
		Accent = Color3.fromRGB(96, 255, 140),
		Info   = Color3.fromRGB(96, 255, 140),
		Scrim  = Color3.fromRGB(2, 10, 4),
		Black  = Color3.fromRGB(8, 22, 12),
		Font       = Font.fromEnum(Enum.Font.Code),
		FontMedium = Font.fromEnum(Enum.Font.Code),
		FontBold   = Font.fromEnum(Enum.Font.Code),
	},

	Midnight = {
		White  = Color3.fromRGB(226, 232, 255),
		Accent = Color3.fromRGB(122, 162, 255),
		Info   = Color3.fromRGB(122, 162, 255),
		Scrim  = Color3.fromRGB(6, 8, 18),
		Black  = Color3.fromRGB(18, 22, 40),
	},

	--- Ink on paper. The one theme that flips the polarity, so it also flips
	--- the surface transparencies to keep contrast.
	Paper = {
		White = Color3.fromRGB(24, 24, 26),
		Black = Color3.fromRGB(248, 248, 250),
		Scrim = Color3.fromRGB(244, 244, 246),
		EmbedColor        = Color3.fromRGB(228, 228, 232),
		EmbedTransparency = 0.15,
		RowTransparency      = 0.92,
		RowHoverTransparency = 0.86,
		RowPressTransparency = 0.80,
		ChipTransparency     = 0.88,
		RuleTransparency     = 0.78,
		Accent = Color3.fromRGB(24, 24, 26),
		Info   = Color3.fromRGB(40, 90, 200),
		Good   = Color3.fromRGB(28, 140, 70),
		Warn   = Color3.fromRGB(180, 110, 0),
		Danger = Color3.fromRGB(200, 40, 40),
	},
}

--- A copy of the defaults, so applying a sparse theme can restore whatever the
--- previous one had changed.
local Defaults = {}

for Key, Value in Theme do
	if Key ~= "Motion" then
		Defaults[Key] = Value
	end
end

local Listeners = {}
local Current = "Remorse"

--- Called after a theme lands, for the handful of things that redraw rather
--- than repaint — gradients, charts, anything built from a colour rather than
--- painted in one.
function Palette.OnChange(Handler)
	table.insert(Listeners, Handler)

	return function()
		local At = table.find(Listeners, Handler)

		if At then
			table.remove(Listeners, At)
		end
	end
end

function Palette.Name()
	return Current
end

--- Applies a theme by name or by table. Every tracked object is repainted, so
--- a live UI changes under you rather than needing a rebuild.
---
--- Repaint is the caller's choice: pass false to change the tokens without
--- touching what is already drawn, which is what you want before the first
--- window is built.
function Palette.Set(Theme_, Repaint)
	local Overlay = Theme_

	if type(Theme_) == "string" then
		Overlay = Palette.Themes[Theme_]

		if not Overlay then
			return false
		end

		Current = Theme_
	else
		Current = "Custom"
	end

	--- Restore first, then overlay, so themes never leak into each other.
	for Key, Value in Defaults do
		Theme[Key] = Value
	end

	for Key, Value in Overlay do
		if Key == "Motion" then
			for Role, Spec in Value do
				Theme.Motion[Role] = Spec
			end
		elseif Key == "Metrics" then
			for Name, Number in Value do
				Metrics[Name] = Number
			end
		else
			Theme[Key] = Value
		end
	end

	if Repaint ~= false then
		for Object, Record in Painted do
			if Object.Parent then
				for Property, Token in Record do
					local Value = Theme[Token]

					--- Fonts and anything non paintable are set outright;
					--- colours and alphas are the only tweened kinds.
					local Ok = pcall(function()
						Object[Property] = Value
					end)

					if not Ok then
						Record[Property] = nil
					end
				end
			else
				Painted[Object] = nil
			end
		end
	end

	for _, Handler in Listeners do
		task.spawn(Handler, Theme)
	end

	return true
end

--- Registers a theme of your own under a name, so it works with SetTheme like
--- any of the built in ones.
function Palette.Register(Name, Overlay)
	Palette.Themes[Name] = Overlay
end

return Palette
Util:
--!nonstrict
--- Util.luau — instance building and the small helpers everything shares.

local Palette = require(script.Parent.Theme)

local Theme   = Palette.Tokens
local Metrics = Palette.Metrics

local Util = {}

--- Builds an instance from a property table and a child list. Parent is
--- applied last so a tree lands in one insertion rather than reflowing per
--- child, and every object passes through the theme tracker on the way out.
local function New(ClassName, Properties, Children)
	local Object = Instance.new(ClassName)

	for Key, Value in Properties or {} do
		if Key ~= "Parent" then
			Object[Key] = Value
		end
	end

	for _, Child in Children or {} do
		Child.Parent = Object
	end

	if Properties then
		Palette.Track(Object, Properties)

		if Properties.Parent then
			Object.Parent = Properties.Parent
		end
	end

	return Object
end

local function Clamp(Value, Minimum, Maximum)
	return math.max(Minimum, math.min(Maximum, Value))
end

local function Quantise(Value, Step)
	if not Step or Step <= 0 then
		return Value
	end

	return math.floor(Value / Step + 0.5) * Step
end

--- Formats to the precision the step implies, with trailing zeroes trimmed, so
--- a 0.05 step reads "1.25" and a 1 step reads "1".
local function FormatNumber(Value, Step)
	if Step and Step < 1 then
		local Decimals = math.max(0, math.ceil(-math.log(Step, 10)))
		local Text = string.format("%." .. Decimals .. "f", Value)

		Text = string.gsub(Text, "%.?0+$", "")

		return Text == "" and "0" or Text
	end

	return tostring(math.floor(Value + 0.5))
end

local function Hex(Colour)
	return string.format("#%02x%02x%02x",
		math.floor(Colour.R * 255 + 0.5),
		math.floor(Colour.G * 255 + 0.5),
		math.floor(Colour.B * 255 + 0.5))
end

--- Mixes toward white or black, for hover and pressed states that have to work
--- against whatever colour the caller passed.
local function Shade(Colour, Amount)
	local Toward = Amount > 0 and 1 or 0
	local Alpha = math.abs(Amount)

	return Color3.new(
		Colour.R + (Toward - Colour.R) * Alpha,
		Colour.G + (Toward - Colour.G) * Alpha,
		Colour.B + (Toward - Colour.B) * Alpha
	)
end

local function Corner(Radius)
	return New("UICorner", { CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, Radius or 0) })
end

local function Padding(Top, Right, Bottom, Left)
	return New("UIPadding", {
		PaddingTop    = UDim.new(0, Top),
		PaddingRight  = UDim.new(0, Right or Top),
		PaddingBottom = UDim.new(0, Bottom or Top),
		PaddingLeft   = UDim.new(0, Left or Right or Top),
	})
end

local function List(Gap, Direction, Alignment)
	return New("UIListLayout", {
		Padding              = UDim.new(0, Gap or 0),
		FillDirection        = Direction or Enum.FillDirection.Vertical,
		SortOrder            = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder,
		HorizontalAlignment  = Alignment or Enum.HorizontalAlignment.Left,
	})
end

--- A horizontal strip layout, since it is the second most common thing built.
local function Strip(Gap, Alignment, Cross)
	return New("UIListLayout", {
		Padding             = UDim.new(0, Gap or 0),
		FillDirection       = Enum.FillDirection.Horizontal,
		SortOrder           = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder,
		HorizontalAlignment = Alignment or Enum.HorizontalAlignment.Left,
		VerticalAlignment   = Cross or Enum.VerticalAlignment.Center,
	})
end

local function Stroke(Colour, Transparency, Thickness)
	return New("UIStroke", {
		Color        = Colour or Theme.White,
		Transparency = Transparency == nil and 0.7 or Transparency,
		Thickness    = Thickness or Metrics.StrokeThickness,
		ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border,
	})
end

--- One pixel of rule. The bracket that frames half the library.
local function Rule(Parent, Anchor, LayoutOrder)
	return New("Frame", {
		Name                   = "Rule",
		Parent                 = Parent,
		BackgroundColor3       = Theme.White,
		BackgroundTransparency = Theme.RuleTransparency,
		BorderSizePixel        = 0,
		AnchorPoint            = Anchor or Vector2.new(0, 0),
		Size                   = UDim2.new(0, 1, 1, 0),
		LayoutOrder            = LayoutOrder or 0,
		ZIndex                 = 2,
	})
end

--- A TextLabel with the library defaults already on it.
local function Text(Properties)
	local Label = New("TextLabel", {
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		BorderSizePixel        = 0,
		TextColor3             = Theme.White,
		TextXAlignment         = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left,
		TextYAlignment         = Enum.TextYAlignment.Top,
		FontFace               = Theme.Font,
		TextSize               = Metrics.RowLabelSize,
		RichText               = true,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0),
		AutomaticSize          = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y,
	})

	for Key, Value in Properties or {} do
		if Key ~= "Parent" then
			Label[Key] = Value
		end
	end

	if Properties then
		Palette.Track(Label, Properties)

		if Properties.Parent then
			Label.Parent = Properties.Parent
		end
	end

	return Label
end

--- Three stacked bars: the log bullet and the menu mark.
local function Glyph(Parent, Size, Alpha)
	local Holder = New("Frame", {
		Name                   = "Glyph",
		Parent                 = Parent,
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(0, Size, 0, Size),
	})

	local Widths = { 1.0, 0.7, 0.85 }

	for Index, Fraction in Widths do
		New("Frame", {
			Name                   = "Bar" .. Index,
			Parent                 = Holder,
			BackgroundColor3       = Theme.White,
			BackgroundTransparency = Alpha or Theme.TextTertiary,
			BorderSizePixel        = 0,
			Position               = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, math.floor(Size * 0.28) + (Index - 1) * 3),
			Size                   = UDim2.new(Fraction, 0, 0, 1),
		})
	end

	return Holder
end

--- A drawn key, for the hint rail.
local function Keycap(Parent, Size)
	local Cap = New("Frame", {
		Name                   = "Keycap",
		Parent                 = Parent,
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(0, Size, 0, math.floor(Size * 0.72)),
	}, {
		Corner(2),
		Stroke(Theme.White, Theme.TextTertiary, 1),
	})

	for Index = 1, 2 do
		New("Frame", {
			Parent                 = Cap,
			BackgroundColor3       = Theme.White,
			BackgroundTransparency = Theme.TextTertiary,
			BorderSizePixel        = 0,
			Position               = UDim2.new(0.22, 0, 0.28 + (Index - 1) * 0.28, 0),
			Size                   = UDim2.new(0.56, 0, 0, 1),
		})
	end

	return Cap
end

--- A chevron built from two bars, which is how every arrow in the library is
--- drawn. Returns the holder and the arms so callers can rotate them.
local function Chevron(Parent, Size, Direction, Alpha)
	local Holder = New("Frame", {
		Name                   = "Chevron",
		Parent                 = Parent,
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(0, Size, 0, Size),
	})

	local Arms = {}
	local Vertical = Direction == "Down" or Direction == "Up"
	local Sign = (Direction == "Up" or Direction == "Left") and -1 or 1

	for Index = 1, 2 do
		Arms[Index] = New("Frame", {
			Parent                 = Holder,
			BackgroundColor3       = Theme.White,
			BackgroundTransparency = Alpha or Theme.TextSecondary,
			BorderSizePixel        = 0,
			AnchorPoint            = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5),
			Position               = Vertical
				and UDim2.new(Index == 1 and 0.28 or 0.72, 0, 0.5, 0)
				or UDim2.new(0.5, 0, Index == 1 and 0.3 or 0.7, 0),
			Size                   = UDim2.new(0, math.max(4, Size - 3), 0, 1),
			Rotation               = Sign * (Index == 1 and 45 or -45),
		})
	end

	--- A chevron dropped into a button sits in the middle of it. One dropped
	--- into something that lays its children out is left alone, because a
	--- layout ignores the position but not the anchor, and moving the anchor
	--- would shift it out of its own slot. Anything that wants it somewhere
	--- else sets the anchor and position afterwards, and wins.
	if not (Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIListLayout")
		or Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIGridLayout")) then
		Holder.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
		Holder.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5, 0)
	end

	return Holder, Arms
end

--- Options resolution. Every control runs its radius, colour and gap through
--- these so a caller can override any of them per widget without the control
--- needing to know about it.
local function Radius(Options, Fallback)
	local Wanted = Options and Options.Radius

	if Wanted == nil then
		return Fallback or 0
	end

	return Wanted
end

local function Round(Options, Fallback, Cap)
	--- Fully round elements clamp against PillRadius, so squaring the theme
	--- squares them too.
	return math.min(Radius(Options, Metrics.PillRadius), Cap or Fallback or 999)
end

local function Colour(Options, Fallback)
	return (Options and Options.Color) or Fallback or Theme.Accent
end

--- Resolves a caller supplied surface into a colour and a transparency, which
--- is how every embed decides whether it has a plate behind it.
---
---   Background = false          no plate at all
---   Background = Color3         that colour, opaque unless told otherwise
---   BackgroundTransparency = n  overrides the transparency either way
local function Surface(Options, Fallback, FallbackAlpha)
	Options = Options or {}

	local Wanted = Options.Background
	local Alpha = Options.BackgroundTransparency

	if Wanted == false or Wanted == "None" then
		return Theme.EmbedColor, 1
	end

	if typeof(Wanted) == "Color3" then
		return Wanted, Alpha == nil and 0 or Alpha
	end

	return Fallback or Theme.EmbedColor,
		Alpha == nil and (FallbackAlpha == nil and Theme.EmbedTransparency or FallbackAlpha) or Alpha
end

local SCALE_TYPES = {
	Fit     = Enum.ScaleType.Fit,
	Cover   = Enum.ScaleType.Crop,
	Crop    = Enum.ScaleType.Crop,
	Stretch = Enum.ScaleType.Stretch,
	Tile    = Enum.ScaleType.Tile,
	Slice   = Enum.ScaleType.Slice,
}

local function ScaleType(Value, Fallback)
	if typeof(Value) == "EnumItem" then
		return Value
	end

	return SCALE_TYPES[Value] or Fallback or Enum.ScaleType.Fit
end

--- Turns a user id, an asset id or a bare number into something an ImageLabel
--- will actually load.
local function Asset(Value)
	if type(Value) == "number" then
		return "rbxassetid://" .. Value
	end

	return Value or ""
end

local function Headshot(UserId, Size)
	return string.format("rbxthumb://type=AvatarHeadShot&id=%d&w=%d&h=%d",
		UserId, Size or 60, Size or 60)
end

local function Portrait(UserId, Size)
	return string.format("rbxthumb://type=AvatarBust&id=%d&w=%d&h=%d",
		UserId, Size or 100, Size or 100)
end

--- The nearest ancestor that is not laying its children out.
---
--- A UIListLayout arranges EVERY visible GuiObject child, so anything dropped
--- into one to sit over, behind or beside its content stops being a decoration
--- and becomes another item in the column. Everything that hangs a shape off
--- something else — an edge light, a reveal plate, a wipe bar, an afterimage —
--- climbs past the layout first, and positions itself in the host's own pixels.
---
--- This has cost real bugs three times: gleams turning into rows inside a
--- dropdown, a notice growing by the width of its own underline, and a status
--- chip's two bracket rules ending up side by side in front of the text.
local function Loose(Object)
	local Host = Object and Object.Parent

	while Host do
		local Arranged = false

		for _, Child in Host:GetChildren() do
			if Child:IsA("UIListLayout") or Child:IsA("UIGridLayout") then
				Arranged = true
				break
			end
		end

		if not Arranged then
			return Host
		end

		Host = Host.Parent
	end

	return Object and Object.Parent
end

--- Copies Extra over a clone of Base. Used everywhere a caller's options need
--- merging with a preset without mutating either.
local function Merge(Base, Extra)
	local Out = {}

	for Key, Value in Base or {} do
		Out[Key] = Value
	end

	for Key, Value in Extra or {} do
		Out[Key] = Value
	end

	return Out
end

Util.New          = New
Util.Clamp        = Clamp
Util.Quantise     = Quantise
Util.FormatNumber = FormatNumber
Util.Hex          = Hex
Util.Shade        = Shade
Util.Corner       = Corner
Util.Padding      = Padding
Util.List         = List
Util.Strip        = Strip
Util.Stroke       = Stroke
Util.Rule         = Rule
Util.Text         = Text
Util.Glyph        = Glyph
Util.Keycap       = Keycap
Util.Chevron      = Chevron
Util.Radius       = Radius
Util.Round        = Round
Util.Colour       = Colour
Util.Surface      = Surface
Util.ScaleType    = ScaleType
Util.Asset        = Asset
Util.Headshot     = Headshot
Util.Portrait     = Portrait
Util.Loose        = Loose
Util.Merge        = Merge

return Util
Window:
--!nonstrict
--- Window.luau — the panel everything lives in.
---
--- A window is deliberately not just a dialog. Strip the chrome, turn off the
--- backdrop and the scroller, park it in a corner, and the same object is a
--- health bar or an ammo counter. Everything that used to be assumed — that it
--- is centred, that it dims the world, that it scrolls — is an option.

local RunService       = game:GetService("RunService")
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
local Lighting         = game:GetService("Lighting")

local Palette = require(script.Parent.Theme)
local Util    = require(script.Parent.Util)
local Motion  = require(script.Parent.Motion)
local Parts   = require(script.Parent.Parts)
local Scroll  = require(script.Parent.Scroll)
local Screen  = require(script.Parent.Screen)
local Reveal  = require(script.Parent.Reveal)
local Layout  = require(script.Parent.Layout)
local Shared  = require(script.Parent.Shared)

local Theme   = Palette.Tokens
local Metrics = Palette.Metrics

local New     = Util.New
local Text    = Util.Text
local Corner  = Util.Corner
local Padding = Util.Padding
local List    = Util.List
local Stroke  = Util.Stroke
local Clamp   = Util.Clamp

local Tween      = Motion.Tween
local MotionTime = Motion.MotionTime
local SwapText   = Motion.SwapText

local Attach = Layout.Attach

--- Where a window parks. Each entry is an anchor point and the position that
--- goes with it, so docking is one lookup rather than nine branches.
local DOCKS = {
	Center      = { Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5), UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5, 0) },
	Top         = { Vector2.new(0.5, 0),   UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, 0) },
	Bottom      = { Vector2.new(0.5, 1),   UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1, 0) },
	Left        = { Vector2.new(0, 0.5),   UDim2.new(0, 0, 0.5, 0) },
	Right       = { Vector2.new(1, 0.5),   UDim2.new(1, 0, 0.5, 0) },
	TopLeft     = { Vector2.new(0, 0),     UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0) },
	TopRight    = { Vector2.new(1, 0),     UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0) },
	BottomLeft  = { Vector2.new(0, 1),     UDim2.new(0, 0, 1, 0) },
	BottomRight = { Vector2.new(1, 1),     UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0) },
}

local function MakeWindow(Options)
	Options = Options or {}

	local Window = {}
	local Order = 0
	local Shown = false
	local Destroyed = false
	local Opening = nil
	local Leaving_ = nil
	local Plated = false

	local Blur = nil
	local ParallaxConnection = nil
	local KeyConnection = nil
	local FitConnection = nil

	local Width  = Options.Width or Metrics.WindowWidth
	local Height = Options.Height or Metrics.WindowHeight

	--- Chrome is the frame: the side rules, the header, the inner padding.
	--- A HUD panel has none of it.
	local Variant = Options.Variant or (Options.Chrome == false and "Bare") or "Rules"
	local Bare = Variant == "Bare" or Variant == "Panel"
	local Scrolls = Options.Scroll ~= false and not Bare or Options.Scroll == true
	local Wash = Options.Wash == nil and (Bare and 1 or 0.55) or Options.Wash
	local BlurSize = Options.Blur == nil and (Bare and 0 or 22) or Options.Blur
	local Padded = Options.Padding == nil and (Bare and 0 or Metrics.WindowPadding - 14) or Options.Padding

	local Dock = DOCKS[Options.Dock or "Center"] or DOCKS.Center
	local Anchor = Options.AnchorPoint or Dock[1]

	--- The resting position, before parallax or a drag moves it. Everything
	--- that repositions the window goes through here so the two never fight.
	local Base = Options.Position or Dock[2]
	local Drift = Vector2.zero

	local Backdrop = New("Frame", {
		Name                   = "Backdrop",
		Parent                 = Screen.Get(),
		BackgroundColor3       = Options.WashColor or Theme.Scrim,
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		BorderSizePixel        = 0,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0),
		Visible                = false,
		ZIndex                 = 1,
	})

	--- The whole window. The layer ignores the top bar inset, which leaves a
	--- strip of exactly that height uncovered along the bottom unless a full
	--- bleed thing is made a bar taller than it looks.
	Screen.Cover(Backdrop)

	if Options.Backdrop == false or Wash >= 1 then
		Backdrop:Destroy()
		Backdrop = nil
	end

	local Root = New("Frame", {
		Name                   = Options.Name or "Window",
		Parent                 = Options.Parent or Screen.Get(),
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		AnchorPoint            = Anchor,
		Position               = Base,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(0, Width, 0, Height),
		Visible                = false,
		ZIndex                 = Options.ZIndex or 2,
	})

	--- A CanvasGroup so the whole panel can fade as one. It rasterises to its
	--- own bounds, so anything that has to escape the window — a dropdown
	--- menu, a child card — is parented to Root or the overlay, never here.
	local Group = New("CanvasGroup", {
		Name                   = "Group",
		Parent                 = Root,
		BackgroundColor3       = Options.Fill or Theme.Scrim,
		BackgroundTransparency = Options.FillTransparency == nil and 1 or Options.FillTransparency,
		BorderSizePixel        = 0,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0),
		GroupTransparency      = 1,
	}, Options.Radius and { Corner(Options.Radius) } or nil)

	if Variant == "Card" then
		Group.BackgroundTransparency = Options.FillTransparency or 0.08
		Corner(Util.Radius(Options, Metrics.CardRadius)).Parent = Group
		Stroke(Theme.White, 0.85, 1).Parent = Group
	end

	--- A window is mostly transparent frames, and a plain Frame does not take
	--- input — so a click on the empty part of one used to sail straight
	--- through to whatever window was underneath, and so did hover. This is a
	--- button filling the panel, below everything else in it, whose only job is
	--- to swallow what lands on this window. Windows stop leaking into each
	--- other, and a covered control stops answering the pointer.
	local Shield = nil

	if Options.Shield ~= false then
		Shield = New("TextButton", {
			Name                   = "Shield",
			Parent                 = Group,
			Text                   = "",
			AutoButtonColor        = false,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			BorderSizePixel        = 0,
			Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0),
			ZIndex                 = 0,
			Modal                  = false,
		})
	end

	local LeftRule, RightRule = nil, nil

	if Variant == "Rules" then
		local function Side(Side_)
			return New("Frame", {
				Name                   = Side_ == 0 and "LeftRule" or "RightRule",
				Parent                 = Group,
				BackgroundColor3       = Theme.White,
				BackgroundTransparency = Theme.RuleTransparency,
				BorderSizePixel        = 0,
				AnchorPoint            = Vector2.new(Side_, 0.5),
				Position               = UDim2.new(Side_, 0, 0.5, 0),
				Size                   = UDim2.new(0, 1, 0, 0),
				ZIndex                 = 3,
			})
		end

		LeftRule, RightRule = Side(0), Side(1)
	end

	local Content = New("Frame", {
		Name                   = "Content",
		Parent                 = Group,
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0),
		ClipsDescendants       = Options.Clip ~= false,
	}, {
		Padding(Options.PaddingTop or (Bare and 0 or 20), Padded,
			Options.PaddingBottom or (Bare and 0 or 14), Padded),
	})

	local Header, Title, Subtitle = nil, nil, nil

	if Options.Title or Options.Subtitle then
		Header = New("Frame", {
			Name                   = "Header",
			Parent                 = Content,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0),
			AutomaticSize          = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y,
		}, {
			Padding(0, Metrics.RowPadding),
			List(1),
		})

		Title = Text({
			Parent      = Header,
			Text        = Options.Title or "",
			TextSize    = Options.TitleSize or Metrics.TitleSize,
			TextWrapped = true,
			LayoutOrder = 1,
		})

		if Options.Subtitle then
			Subtitle = Text({
				Parent           = Header,
				Text             = Options.Subtitle,
				TextSize         = Options.SubtitleSize or Metrics.SubtitleSize,
				TextTransparency = Theme.TextSecondary,
				TextWrapped      = true,
				LayoutOrder      = 2,
			})
		end
	end

	--- A title bar: a rule, a name, and the three controls a desktop window
	--- has. Off by default, because most of what this library draws is not a
	--- desktop window.
	local TitleBar, Controls_ = nil, {}

	if Options.TitleBar then
		TitleBar = New("Frame", {
			Name                   = "TitleBar",
			Parent                 = Content,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 22),
			ZIndex                 = 6,
		}, {
			Padding(0, Metrics.RowPadding),
		})

		Text({
			Parent           = TitleBar,
			Text             = Options.Title or Options.Name or "Window",
			FontFace         = Theme.FontMono,
			TextSize          = Metrics.MonoBoldSize,
			TextTransparency = Theme.TextTertiary,
			TextYAlignment   = Enum.TextYAlignment.Center,
			TextTruncate     = Enum.TextTruncate.AtEnd,
			Size             = UDim2.new(1, -70, 1, 0),
			AutomaticSize    = Enum.AutomaticSize.None,
		})

		New("Frame", {
			Parent                 = TitleBar,
			BackgroundColor3       = Theme.White,
			BackgroundTransparency = Theme.RuleTransparency,
			BorderSizePixel        = 0,
			AnchorPoint            = Vector2.new(0, 1),
			Position               = UDim2.new(0, 0, 1, 0),
			Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 1),
		})

		local Buttons = New("Frame", {
			Parent                 = TitleBar,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			AnchorPoint            = Vector2.new(1, 0.5),
			Position               = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0.5, 0),
			Size                   = UDim2.new(0, 60, 1, 0),
			ZIndex                 = 7,
		}, {
			New("UIListLayout", {
				Padding             = UDim.new(0, 6),
				FillDirection       = Enum.FillDirection.Horizontal,
				SortOrder           = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder,
				HorizontalAlignment = Enum.HorizontalAlignment.Right,
				VerticalAlignment   = Enum.VerticalAlignment.Center,
			}),
		})

		--- Each control is a glyph drawn from rules, in the house style: a
		--- bar, a box, a cross.
		local function Control(Order, Kind, OnPress)
			local Button = New("TextButton", {
				Name                   = Kind,
				Parent                 = Buttons,
				BackgroundTransparency = 1,
				Text                   = "",
				AutoButtonColor        = false,
				Size                   = UDim2.new(0, 14, 0, 14),
				LayoutOrder            = Order,
				ZIndex                 = 8,
			})

			if Kind == "Minimise" then
				New("Frame", {
					Parent                 = Button,
					BackgroundColor3       = Theme.White,
					BackgroundTransparency = Theme.TextSecondary,
					BorderSizePixel        = 0,
					AnchorPoint            = Vector2.new(0.5, 1),
					Position               = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1, -3),
					Size                   = UDim2.new(0, 10, 0, 1),
				})
			elseif Kind == "Maximise" then
				New("Frame", {
					Parent                 = Button,
					BackgroundTransparency = 1,
					AnchorPoint            = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5),
					Position               = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5, 0),
					Size                   = UDim2.new(0, 10, 0, 10),
				}, {
					Stroke(Theme.White, Theme.TextSecondary, 1),
				})
			else
				for Arm = 1, 2 do
					New("Frame", {
						Parent                 = Button,
						BackgroundColor3       = Theme.White,
						BackgroundTransparency = Theme.TextSecondary,
						BorderSizePixel        = 0,
						AnchorPoint            = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5),
						Position               = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5, 0),
						Size                   = UDim2.new(0, 11, 0, 1),
						Rotation               = Arm == 1 and 45 or -45,
					})
				end
			end

			Button.Activated:Connect(OnPress)

			Controls_[Kind] = Button

			return Button
		end

		if Options.Minimise ~= false then
			Control(1, "Minimise", function()
				Window:Minimise()
			end)
		end

		if Options.Maximise ~= false then
			Control(2, "Maximise", function()
				Window:Maximise()
			end)
		end

		if Options.Closable ~= false then
			Control(3, "Close", function()
				Window:Close()
			end)
		end
	end

	local Body = nil

	if Scrolls then
		Body = New("ScrollingFrame", {
			Name                   = "Body",
			Parent                 = Content,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			BorderSizePixel        = 0,
			Position               = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0),
			Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0),
			CanvasSize             = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0),
			AutomaticCanvasSize    = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y,
			ScrollBarThickness     = 0,
			ScrollingDirection     = Enum.ScrollingDirection.Y,
			ClipsDescendants       = true,
		}, {
			List(Options.Gap or Metrics.RowGap),
		})

		Window.Scroll = Scroll.Attach(Body, "Y", { Gleam = Options.Gleam })
	else
		Body = New("Frame", {
			Name                   = "Body",
			Parent                 = Content,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			Position               = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0),
			Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0),
			AutomaticSize          = Options.AutoSize and Enum.AutomaticSize.Y or Enum.AutomaticSize.None,
		}, {
			List(Options.Gap or Metrics.RowGap),
		})
	end

	--- The header is auto sized, so the body's top has to follow it rather
	--- than being a constant.
	local StatusBar = nil

	if Options.StatusBar then
		StatusBar = New("Frame", {
			Name                   = "StatusBar",
			Parent                 = Content,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			AnchorPoint            = Vector2.new(0, 1),
			Position               = UDim2.new(0, 0, 1, 0),
			Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 18),
			ZIndex                 = 6,
		}, {
			Padding(0, Metrics.RowPadding),
		})

		New("Frame", {
			Parent                 = StatusBar,
			BackgroundColor3       = Theme.White,
			BackgroundTransparency = Theme.RuleTransparency,
			BorderSizePixel        = 0,
			Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 1),
		})

		--- StatusLabel, not Status: Status is a control, and Attach refuses to
		--- shadow a field with one.
		Window.StatusLabel = Text({
			Parent           = StatusBar,
			Text             = type(Options.StatusBar) == "string" and Options.StatusBar or "",
			FontFace         = Theme.FontMono,
			TextSize         = Metrics.MonoSize,
			TextTransparency = Theme.TextTertiary,
			TextYAlignment   = Enum.TextYAlignment.Center,
			TextTruncate     = Enum.TextTruncate.AtEnd,
			Position         = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 2),
			Size             = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, -2),
			AutomaticSize    = Enum.AutomaticSize.None,
		})
	end

	--- The header is auto sized and the bars are not, so the body's top and
	--- bottom both have to follow rather than being constants.
	local function Reflow()
		local Top = TitleBar and 28 or 0
		local Bottom = StatusBar and 22 or 0

		if Header then
			Header.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, Top)
			Top += Header.AbsoluteSize.Y + 18
		end

		Body.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, Top)
		Body.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, -(Top + Bottom))
	end

	if Header then
		Header:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"):Connect(Reflow)
	end

	task.defer(Reflow)

	--- Modal only unlocks the cursor; it never blocks input. A HUD panel wants
	--- neither, which is why it defaults off for bare windows.
	local Unlock = Options.UnlockMouse

	if Unlock == nil then
		Unlock = not Bare
	end

	local Modal = New("TextButton", {
		Name                   = "Modal",
		Parent                 = Root,
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		Text                   = "",
		AutoButtonColor        = false,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0),
		Modal                  = Unlock,
		Visible                = false,
	})

	--- Popovers land here: a plain frame on top of the group, outside its
	--- rasterisation, so a dropdown can hang past the window's edge.
	local Overlay = New("Frame", {
		Name                   = "Overlay",
		Parent                 = Root,
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0),
		ZIndex                 = 40,
	})

	Window.Root     = Root
	Window.Overlay  = Overlay
	Window.Body     = Body
	Window.Backdrop = Backdrop
	--- Canvas, not Group: Group is a control, and the registry mixed into
	--- every container would overwrite a field of that name.
	Window.Canvas   = Group
	Window.Content  = Content
	Window.HeaderFrame = Header
	Window.TitleBar = TitleBar
	Window.TabBars  = {}
	Window.Options  = Options

	local Poppers = {}
	local Children = {}

	function Window:_Order()
		Order += 1
		return Order
	end

	function Window:_Mount()
		return Body
	end

	function Window:_Overlay()
		return Overlay
	end

	function Window:_Window()
		return Window
	end

	function Window:_Register(Close)
		table.insert(Poppers, Close)
	end

	function Window:_ClosePopovers()
		for _, Close in Poppers do
			Close()
		end
	end

	function Window:Section(Title_, Description, SectionOptions)
		return Layout.Section(Window, Title_, Description, SectionOptions)
	end

	function Window:Tabs(TabOptions)
		return Layout.Tabs(Window, TabOptions)
	end

	Window._MakeTabs = Window.Tabs

	function Window:IsOpen()
		return Shown
	end

	function Window:Open()
		if Shown or Destroyed then
			return Window
		end

		Shown = true
		Root.Visible = true
		Modal.Visible = true

		--- A window always opens at the top of its content, whatever was built
		--- into it or scrolled to last time.
		if Window.Scroll then
			Window.Scroll:Top()
		elseif Body:IsA("ScrollingFrame") then
			Body.CanvasPosition = Vector2.zero
		end

		if Backdrop then
			Backdrop.Visible = true
			Tween(Backdrop, { BackgroundTransparency = Wash }, "enter")
		end

		if BlurSize > 0 then
			if not Blur then
				Blur = New("BlurEffect", { Parent = Lighting, Size = 0, Name = "KuikBlur" })
			end

			Tween(Blur, { Size = BlurSize }, "enter")
		end

		--- A window can arrive as a white plate that becomes it, rather than by
		--- fading up. The plate is measured against Root, so it is exactly the
		--- window's rectangle however the window is sized.
		---
		--- On by default for anything that is a panel, off for anything that is
		--- not: a HUD element stripped of its chrome should open without
		--- ceremony, and flashing white every time a health bar appears would be
		--- ridiculous. Reveal = false turns it off anywhere.
		local Wants = Options.Reveal

		if Wants == nil then
			Wants = Metrics.Reveal and not Bare
		end

		if Wants then
			local Setting = type(Wants) == "table" and Wants or {}

			local function Try()
				if Opening then
					Opening.Cancel()
				end

				Opening = Reveal.Plate(Group, {
					Parent = Root,
					Now    = true,
					To     = 0,
					Radius = Options.Radius or (Variant == "Card" and Metrics.CardRadius or 0),
					Color  = Setting.Color,
					From   = Setting.From or Options.RevealFrom,
					Drift  = Setting.Drift,
				})

				--- A plate refuses anything it cannot measure. Without the
				--- fallback the window would simply never appear.
				Plated = Opening ~= nil and Opening.Face ~= nil

				if not Plated then
					Tween(Group, { GroupTransparency = 0 }, "enter")
				end
			end

			if Root.AbsoluteSize.X > 2 then
				Try()
			else
				--- Built and opened in the same breath, which is what
				--- Open = true does and what a deck of cards does. Nothing has
				--- been laid out yet, so wait a frame for a size rather than
				--- giving up on the reveal entirely.
				task.defer(function()
					if Shown and not Destroyed then
						Try()
					end
				end)
			end
		else
			Tween(Group, { GroupTransparency = 0 }, "enter")
		end

		if LeftRule then
			Tween(LeftRule, { Size = UDim2.new(0, 1, 1, 0) }, "reveal")
			Tween(RightRule, { Size = UDim2.new(0, 1, 1, 0) }, "reveal")
		end

		if Options.Opened then
			task.spawn(Options.Opened, Window)
		end

		return Window
	end

	function Window:Close()
		if not Shown or Destroyed then
			return Window
		end

		if Leaving_ then
			Leaving_.Cancel()
			Leaving_ = nil
		end

		Window:_ClosePopovers()

		for _, Child in Children do
			Child:Close()
		end

		Shown = false
		Modal.Visible = false

		if Blur then
			Tween(Blur, { Size = 0 }, "exit")
		end

		if Backdrop then
			Tween(Backdrop, { BackgroundTransparency = 1 }, "exit")
		end

		--- A window that arrived as a plate leaves under one: the same white
		--- comes back over it and shuts. Anything that opened by fading up
		--- fades back down, so the two halves always match.
		local Handle = nil

		if Opening or Plated then
			if Opening then
				Opening.Cancel()
				Opening = nil
			end

			Plated = false

			local Setting = type(Options.Reveal) == "table" and Options.Reveal or {}

			Leaving_ = Reveal.Cover(Group, {
				Parent = Root,
				Radius = Options.Radius or (Variant == "Card" and Metrics.CardRadius or 0),
				Color  = Setting.Color,
			})
		end

		if not Leaving_ or not Leaving_.Face then
			Handle = Tween(Group, { GroupTransparency = 1 }, "exit")
		end

		if LeftRule then
			Tween(LeftRule, { Size = UDim2.new(0, 1, 0, 0) }, "exit")
			Handle = Tween(RightRule, { Size = UDim2.new(0, 1, 0, 0) }, "exit")
		end

		Handle.Completed:Once(function()
			if not Shown then
				Root.Visible = false

				if Backdrop then
					Backdrop.Visible = false
				end
			end
		end)

		if Options.Closed then
			task.spawn(Options.Closed, Window)
		end

		return Window
	end

	function Window:SetOpen(Open)
		if Open then
			return Window:Open()
		end

		return Window:Close()
	end

	--- No Window:Toggle: Toggle is a control, and the registry mixed into
	--- every container owns that name. SetOpen is the verb.
	Window.Show = Window.Open
	Window.Hide = Window.Close

	--- Position, size and anchor, all live and all animated by default. This
	--- is what makes a window usable as a HUD element rather than a dialog.
	--- Never above the top of the screen.
	---
	--- The layer ignores the top bar inset, so it starts one inset ABOVE what
	--- the player can see — and a window placed at "24 from the top" therefore
	--- lands at -34 and loses its title bar off the edge. That is what made a
	--- window with chrome open looking like an empty rectangle.
	---
	--- Only the top is guarded, and only for a window anchored near it: a HUD
	--- element deliberately hung off the bottom or bled off an edge is doing
	--- that on purpose.
	local function Clear(Target)
		if Options.Safe == false or Root.AnchorPoint.Y > 0.5 then
			return Target
		end

		local Top = Screen.Inset()

		if Top <= 0 or Target.Y.Scale > 0.5 then
			return Target
		end

		local Tall = Screen.Get().AbsoluteSize.Y
		local At = Target.Y.Scale * Tall + Target.Y.Offset
		local Above = At - Root.AnchorPoint.Y * Root.AbsoluteSize.Y

		if Above >= Top then
			return Target
		end

		return UDim2.new(
			Target.X.Scale, Target.X.Offset,
			Target.Y.Scale, Target.Y.Offset + (Top - Above))
	end

	local function Land(Animate)
		local Target = Clear(UDim2.new(
			Base.X.Scale, Base.X.Offset + Drift.X,
			Base.Y.Scale, Base.Y.Offset + Drift.Y))

		if Animate == false then
			--- A spring already running on this property would keep writing to
			--- it every frame and quietly undo the assignment. Setting a value
			--- outright has to stop whatever was moving it.
			Motion.Halt(Root, "Position")
			Root.Position = Target
		else
			Tween(Root, { Position = Target }, Animate == true and "layout" or Animate)
		end
	end

	function Window:SetPosition(Position, Animate)
		Base = Position
		Land(Animate)
		return Window
	end

	function Window:GetPosition()
		return Base
	end

	function Window:SetAnchor(Point)
		Root.AnchorPoint = Point
		return Window
	end

	function Window:SetSize(NewWidth, NewHeight, Animate)
		Width = NewWidth or Width
		Height = NewHeight or Height

		local Target = UDim2.new(0, Width, 0, Height)

		if Animate == false then
			Motion.Halt(Root, "Size")
			Root.Size = Target
		else
			Tween(Root, { Size = Target }, Animate == true and "layout" or Animate)
		end

		return Window
	end

	function Window:GetSize()
		return Width, Height
	end

	--- Parks the window against an edge or a corner, optionally inset.
	function Window:Dock(Where, Inset, Animate)
		local Spot = DOCKS[Where]

		if not Spot then
			return Window
		end

		local Pad = Inset or 0
		local Anchor_ = Spot[1]

		Root.AnchorPoint = Anchor_

		Base = UDim2.new(
			Spot[2].X.Scale,
			Spot[2].X.Offset + (Anchor_.X == 0 and Pad or Anchor_.X == 1 and -Pad or 0),
			Spot[2].Y.Scale,
			Spot[2].Y.Offset + (Anchor_.Y == 0 and Pad or Anchor_.Y == 1 and -Pad or 0))

		Land(Animate)

		return Window
	end

	--- Nudges the window by a pixel offset from wherever it is.
	function Window:Nudge(X, Y, Animate)
		Base = UDim2.new(Base.X.Scale, Base.X.Offset + X, Base.Y.Scale, Base.Y.Offset + Y)
		Land(Animate)
		return Window
	end

	function Window:SetScale(Scale, Animate)
		local Handle = Root:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIScale")
			or New("UIScale", { Parent = Root, Scale = 1 })

		if Animate == false then
			Motion.Halt(Handle, "Scale")
			Handle.Scale = Scale
		else
			Tween(Handle, { Scale = Scale }, "toss")
		end

		return Window
	end

	function Window:SetOpacity(Alpha, Animate)
		if Animate == false then
			Motion.Halt(Group, "GroupTransparency")
			Group.GroupTransparency = 1 - Alpha
		else
			Tween(Group, { GroupTransparency = 1 - Alpha }, "fade")
		end

		return Window
	end

	function Window:SetZIndex(Value)
		Root.ZIndex = Value
		return Window
	end

	--- Raises the window above its siblings, for a stack of loose panels.
	function Window:BringToFront()
		local Highest = 0

		for _, Sibling in Root.Parent:GetChildren() do
			if Sibling:IsA("GuiObject") and Sibling ~= Root then
				Highest = math.max(Highest, Sibling.ZIndex)
			end
		end

		Root.ZIndex = Highest + 1

		return Window
	end

	--- Collapsed to its title bar, and back. Remembers the size it had, so
	--- restoring lands where it started rather than at the default.
	local Restored = nil

	function Window:Minimise()
		if Restored then
			return Window:Restore()
		end

		Restored = { Width = Width, Height = Height }
		Window:SetSize(Width, TitleBar and 28 or 34)

		return Window
	end

	function Window:Maximise()
		local Viewport = Screen.Get().AbsoluteSize

		if Restored then
			return Window:Restore()
		end

		Restored = { Width = Width, Height = Height }
		Window:SetSize(math.max(200, Viewport.X - 60), math.max(160, Viewport.Y - 80))

		return Window
	end

	function Window:Restore()
		if not Restored then
			return Window
		end

		Window:SetSize(Restored.Width, Restored.Height)
		Restored = nil

		return Window
	end

	function Window:IsRestored()
		return Restored == nil
	end

	--- The line along the bottom, when there is one.
	function Window:SetStatus(Text_)
		if Window.StatusLabel then
			Window.StatusLabel.Text = Text_
		end

		return Window
	end

	function Window:SetTitle(NewTitle, NewSubtitle)
		if Title and NewTitle then
			SwapText(Title, NewTitle)
		end

		if Subtitle and NewSubtitle then
			SwapText(Subtitle, NewSubtitle)
		end

		return Window
	end

	function Window:SetFill(Colour, Alpha, Animate)
		if Colour then
			Motion.Paint(Group, { BackgroundColor3 = Colour }, Animate)
		end

		if Alpha ~= nil then
			Tween(Group, { BackgroundTransparency = Alpha }, "fade")
		end

		return Window
	end

	--- Dragging. By the header when there is one, by the whole panel when
	--- there is not, which is what a loose HUD element wants.
	local Dragging = nil
	local DragConnections = {}

	function Window:SetDraggable(Enabled, Grip)
		for _, Connection in DragConnections do
			Connection:Disconnect()
		end

		table.clear(DragConnections)

		if not Enabled then
			return Window
		end

		local Handle = Grip or TitleBar or Header or Group

		table.insert(DragConnections, Handle.InputBegan:Connect(function(Input)
			if Input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1
				and Input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.Touch then
				return
			end

			Dragging = {
				Start = Input.Position,
				Origin = Base,
			}

			Window:BringToFront()
		end))

		table.insert(DragConnections, UserInputService.InputChanged:Connect(function(Input)
			if not Dragging then
				return
			end

			if Input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.MouseMovement
				and Input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.Touch then
				return
			end

			local Delta = Input.Position - Dragging.Start

			Base = UDim2.new(
				Dragging.Origin.X.Scale, Dragging.Origin.X.Offset + Delta.X,
				Dragging.Origin.Y.Scale, Dragging.Origin.Y.Offset + Delta.Y)

			--- Sprung rather than assigned, so the panel has weight instead of
			--- sticking to the cursor.
			Land("drag")
		end))

		table.insert(DragConnections, UserInputService.InputEnded:Connect(function(Input)
			if Dragging and (Input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1
				or Input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch) then
				Dragging = nil

				if Options.Moved then
					task.spawn(Options.Moved, Base)
				end
			end
		end))

		return Window
	end

	--- A grip in the bottom right corner. Two rules, because that is what
	--- everything else in the library is made of.
	local Grip = nil

	function Window:SetResizable(Enabled)
		if not Enabled then
			if Grip then
				Grip:Destroy()
				Grip = nil
			end

			return Window
		end

		if Grip then
			return Window
		end

		Grip = New("TextButton", {
			Name                   = "Grip",
			Parent                 = Root,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			Text                   = "",
			AutoButtonColor        = false,
			AnchorPoint            = Vector2.new(1, 1),
			Position               = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0),
			Size                   = UDim2.new(0, 16, 0, 16),
			ZIndex                 = 45,
		})

		for Index = 1, 2 do
			New("Frame", {
				Parent                 = Grip,
				BackgroundColor3       = Theme.White,
				BackgroundTransparency = Theme.RuleTransparency,
				BorderSizePixel        = 0,
				AnchorPoint            = Vector2.new(1, 1),
				Position               = UDim2.new(1, -2, 1, -2),
				Size                   = Index == 1
					and UDim2.new(0, 10, 0, 1)
					or UDim2.new(0, 1, 0, 10),
			})
		end

		local Sizing = nil

		Grip.InputBegan:Connect(function(Input)
			if Input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1
				or Input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch then
				Sizing = { Start = Input.Position, Width = Width, Height = Height }
			end
		end)

		table.insert(DragConnections, UserInputService.InputChanged:Connect(function(Input)
			if not Sizing then
				return
			end

			if Input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.MouseMovement
				and Input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.Touch then
				return
			end

			local Delta = Input.Position - Sizing.Start

			Window:SetSize(
				math.max(Options.MinWidth or 160, Sizing.Width + Delta.X),
				math.max(Options.MinHeight or 120, Sizing.Height + Delta.Y),
				"drag")
		end))

		table.insert(DragConnections, UserInputService.InputEnded:Connect(function(Input)
			if Sizing and (Input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1
				or Input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch) then
				Sizing = nil

				if Options.Resized then
					task.spawn(Options.Resized, Width, Height)
				end
			end
		end))

		return Window
	end

	--- Parallax: the panel lags behind the camera and settles back.
	---
	--- The offset is sprung to rather than assigned, so a fast flick reads as
	--- the window being dragged along rather than teleporting.
	function Window:SetParallax(Amount)
		if ParallaxConnection then
			ParallaxConnection:Disconnect()
			ParallaxConnection = nil
		end

		if not Amount or Amount <= 0 then
			Drift = Vector2.zero
			Land("layout")
			return Window
		end

		local Offset = Vector2.zero
		local LastYaw, LastPitch = nil, nil

		ParallaxConnection = RunService.RenderStepped:Connect(function(Delta)
			local Camera = workspace.CurrentCamera

			if not Camera then
				return
			end

			local Look = Camera.CFrame.LookVector
			local Yaw = math.atan2(-Look.X, -Look.Z)
			local Pitch = math.asin(Clamp(Look.Y, -1, 1))

			if LastYaw then
				local YawDelta = Yaw - LastYaw

				--- Wrap the short way, or spinning past due south throws the
				--- panel across the screen.
				if YawDelta > math.pi then
					YawDelta -= math.pi * 2
				elseif YawDelta < -math.pi then
					YawDelta += math.pi * 2
				end

				Offset += Vector2.new(YawDelta, Pitch - LastPitch) * Amount * 30
			end

			LastYaw, LastPitch = Yaw, Pitch

			Offset = Offset:Lerp(Vector2.zero, math.min(1, Delta * 7))

			Drift = Vector2.new(
				Clamp(Offset.X, -Amount, Amount),
				Clamp(Offset.Y, -Amount, Amount))

			Land("drag")
		end)

		return Window
	end

	--- Selects the named page on whichever tab bar owns it.
	function Window:GoTo(Name)
		for _, Bar in Window.TabBars do
			if Bar:Pages()[Name] then
				Bar:Select(Name)
				return true
			end
		end

		return false
	end

	--- Scrolls something into view and flashes it, so a link that points at a
	--- setting three pages down actually lands you on it.
	function Window:Reveal(Target)
		local Frame = typeof(Target) == "Instance" and Target
			or (type(Target) == "table" and Target.Frame)

		if not Frame then
			return false
		end

		--- Walk up to whichever page holds it and select that first.
		local Node = Frame

		while Node and Node ~= Body do
			if string.sub(Node.Name, 1, 5) == "Page_" then
				Window:GoTo(string.sub(Node.Name, 6))
				break
			end

			Node = Node.Parent
		end

		task.defer(function()
			if not Body:IsA("ScrollingFrame") then
				return
			end

			local Offset = Frame.AbsolutePosition.Y - Body.AbsolutePosition.Y + Body.CanvasPosition.Y
			local Span = math.max(0, Body.AbsoluteCanvasSize.Y - Body.AbsoluteSize.Y)
			local To = Clamp(Offset - Body.AbsoluteSize.Y / 3, 0, Span)

			if Window.Scroll then
				Window.Scroll:To(Vector2.new(0, To))
			else
				Body.CanvasPosition = Vector2.new(0, To)
			end

			--- A double pulse of the row fill: enough to find it, not enough
			--- to be a strobe.
			if Frame:IsA("GuiObject") then
				for Index = 1, 2 do
					task.delay(MotionTime("scroll") + (Index - 1) * 0.24, function()
						Tween(Frame, { BackgroundTransparency = 0.7 }, "hover")

						task.delay(0.12, function()
							Tween(Frame, { BackgroundTransparency = Theme.RowTransparency }, "fade")
						end)
					end)
				end
			end
		end)

		return true
	end

	--- A sub window, parked beside this one. Parented to Root rather than the
	--- group, because the group rasterises to its own bounds and would clip it.
	function Window:Child(ChildOptions)
		ChildOptions = ChildOptions or {}

		local Child = MakeWindow(Util.Merge(ChildOptions, {
			Width       = ChildOptions.Width or 300,
			Height      = ChildOptions.Height or 320,
			Blur        = ChildOptions.Blur or 0,
			Wash        = ChildOptions.Wash or 1,
			UnlockMouse = false,
			Parent      = Root,
		}))

		Child.Root.AnchorPoint = ChildOptions.AnchorPoint or Vector2.new(0, 0.5)
		Child:SetPosition(ChildOptions.Position
			or UDim2.new(1, ChildOptions.Offset or 34, 0.5, 0), false)

		if Child.Backdrop then
			Child.Backdrop:Destroy()
			Child.Backdrop = nil
		end

		Child.Owner = Window
		table.insert(Children, Child)

		--- Detach on destroy, or a window that outlives several editors ends
		--- up iterating a list of dead ones.
		Child:OnDestroy(function()
			local At = table.find(Children, Child)

			if At then
				table.remove(Children, At)
			end
		end)

		if ChildOptions.Open then
			Child:Open()
		end

		return Child
	end

	function Window:Children()
		return Children
	end

	local Closing = {}

	function Window:OnDestroy(Handler)
		table.insert(Closing, Handler)
		return Window
	end

	--- Idempotent: destroying a window twice, or destroying a deck that holds
	--- windows the caller has already destroyed, must not throw.
	local Leaving = false

	--- Destroy is immediate. Pass true and the window shrinks and fades out
	--- first, then tears itself down — explicit, because a window that is still
	--- on screen after the code that closed it has moved on is a bug every
	--- other time.
	function Window:Destroy(Animate)
		if Destroyed then
			return
		end

		if Animate then
			--- Still alive while it leaves — the teardown below is what makes
			--- it dead — but flagged, so a second call during the animation
			--- does not start a second one.
			if Leaving then
				return
			end

			Leaving = true
			Modal.Visible = false

			if Backdrop then
				Tween(Backdrop, { BackgroundTransparency = 1 }, "exit")
			end

			if Blur then
				Tween(Blur, { Size = 0 }, "exit")
			end

			Motion.Out(Root, function()
				Leaving = false
				Window:Destroy()
			end, "shrink")

			return
		end

		Destroyed = true

		for _, Handler in Closing do
			task.spawn(Handler, Window)
		end

		for _, Child in table.clone(Children) do
			Child:Destroy()
		end

		table.clear(Children)

		for _, Connection in DragConnections do
			Connection:Disconnect()
		end

		table.clear(DragConnections)

		if Window.Scroll then
			Window.Scroll:Destroy()
		end

		if ParallaxConnection then
			ParallaxConnection:Disconnect()
		end

		if KeyConnection then
			KeyConnection:Disconnect()
		end

		if FitConnection then
			FitConnection:Disconnect()
		end

		if Blur then
			Blur:Destroy()
		end

		Root:Destroy()

		if Backdrop then
			Backdrop:Destroy()
		end
	end

	function Window:IsAlive()
		return not Destroyed
	end

	--- Keeps a window inside the viewport. Off for anything docked or bare,
	--- since a HUD element sized to its content should be left alone.
	if Options.Fit ~= false and not Bare then
		local function Fit()
			local Viewport = Screen.Get().AbsoluteSize

			if Viewport.X > 0 then
				Root.Size = UDim2.new(
					0, math.min(Width, Viewport.X - 40),
					0, math.min(Height, Viewport.Y - 80))
			end

			--- And put it back where it belongs, which is what applies the top
			--- guard. The initial position is written straight onto Root when
			--- the window is built, before there is a size to guard against —
			--- so without this a window docked to the top keeps the placement
			--- that hid its own title bar above the screen.
			Land(false)
		end

		FitConnection = Screen.Get():GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"):Connect(Fit)
		task.defer(Fit)
	else
		task.defer(function()
			if not Destroyed then
				Land(false)
			end
		end)
	end

	if Options.Key then
		KeyConnection = UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(Input, Processed)
			--- A prompt owns the keyboard while it is up.
			if not Processed and not Screen.Blocked() and Input.KeyCode == Options.Key then
				Window:SetOpen(not Shown)
			end
		end)
	end

	if Options.Draggable then
		Window:SetDraggable(true, Options.Grip)
	end

	if Options.Resizable then
		Window:SetResizable(true)
	end

	if Options.Parallax then
		Window:SetParallax(Options.Parallax)
	end

	if Options.Open then
		task.defer(function()
			Window:Open()
		end)
	end

	return Attach(Window)
end

Shared.Window = MakeWindow

return MakeWindow
--!nonstrict
--- Kuik — a Roblox UI library in the NO REMORSE house style.
---
--- Rules and type, almost no fill, square by default, and everything moving on
--- springs. Built out of small modules: Theme is the tokens, Motion is the
--- spring solver, Parts is the two shells every control is made of, and
--- Controls is the registry that gets mixed into every container.
---
---   local Kuik = require(path.to.Kuik)
---
---   local Window = Kuik.Window({ Title = "Settings", Key = Enum.KeyCode.RightShift })
---   local Page = Window:Tabs():Page("Audio")
---
---   Page:Slider({ Label = "Master", Min = 0, Max = 100, Default = 80 })

local Palette  = require(script.Theme)
local Util     = require(script.Util)
local Motion   = require(script.Motion)
local Parts    = require(script.Parts)
local Scroll   = require(script.Scroll)
local Screen   = require(script.Screen)
local Controls = require(script.Controls)
local Layout   = require(script.Layout)
local Window   = require(script.Window)
local Hud      = require(script.Hud)
local Layers   = require(script.Layers)
local Reveal   = require(script.Reveal)

local Kuik = {}

Kuik.Version = {
	Name    = "Kuik",
	Version = "2.0.0",
}

--- Live token tables. Mutated in place by SetTheme, so anything holding a
--- reference keeps seeing the current values.
Kuik.Theme   = Palette.Tokens
Kuik.Metrics = Palette.Metrics
Kuik.Themes  = Palette.Themes

--- Windows and panels ------------------------------------------------------

Kuik.Window = Window

--- A window with the chrome stripped: no header, no side rules, no backdrop,
--- no blur, no scroller, and it does not unlock the mouse. This is the one to
--- build a health bar or an ammo counter out of.
function Kuik.Panel(Options)
	return Window(Util.Merge({
		Variant     = "Bare",
		Wash        = 1,
		Blur        = 0,
		Backdrop    = false,
		UnlockMouse = false,
		Scroll      = false,
		Fit         = false,
		Open        = true,
		Width       = 220,
		Height      = 80,
	}, Options))
end

--- A window that looks like a card: filled, rounded, stroked.
function Kuik.Card(Options)
	return Window(Util.Merge({ Variant = "Card" }, Options))
end

--- Layers ------------------------------------------------------------------

Kuik.Menu    = Layers.Menu
Kuik.Prompt  = Layers.Prompt
Kuik.Cards   = Layers.Cards
Kuik.Popover = Layers.Popover
Kuik.Sheet   = Layers.Sheet
Kuik.Drawer  = Layers.Drawer
Kuik.Coach   = Layers.Coach

--- HUD ---------------------------------------------------------------------

Kuik.Toast     = Hud.Toast
Kuik.Notify    = Hud.Notify
Kuik.Hints     = Hud.Hints
Kuik.Log       = Hud.Log
Kuik.Arrival   = Hud.Arrival
Kuik.Feed      = Hud.Feed
Kuik.Console   = Hud.Console
Kuik.Watermark = Hud.Watermark
Kuik.Bar       = Hud.Bar
Kuik.Timer     = Hud.Timer
Kuik.Ammo      = Hud.Ammo
Kuik.Crosshair = Hud.Crosshair
Kuik.Killfeed  = Hud.Killfeed
Kuik.Objective = Hud.Objective
Kuik.Vignette  = Hud.Vignette
Kuik.Compass   = Hud.Compass
Kuik.Fab       = Hud.Fab
Kuik.Viewfinder = Hud.Viewfinder

--- Reticle is the same thing a Crosshair is, under the name a 3D UI uses.
Kuik.Reticle   = Hud.Crosshair

--- Theming -----------------------------------------------------------------

--- Applies a theme by name or by table, repainting whatever is already on
--- screen. Pass Repaint = false to change the tokens only.
function Kuik.SetTheme(Theme, Repaint)
	return Palette.Set(Theme, Repaint)
end

function Kuik.GetTheme()
	return Palette.Name()
end

--- Registers a theme of your own under a name.
function Kuik.RegisterTheme(Name, Overlay)
	Palette.Register(Name, Overlay)
	return Kuik
end

--- Called after any theme change, for anything built from a colour rather than
--- painted in one.
function Kuik.OnTheme(Handler)
	return Palette.OnChange(Handler)
end

--- Extension ---------------------------------------------------------------

--- The control registry. Every name in here is a method on every container.
Kuik.Controls = Controls

--- Adds a control of your own. It becomes a method on every container built
--- after this call, so register before you build.
---
---   Kuik.Register("Sticker", function(Container, Options, Owner)
---       ... return Handle
---   end)
---
---   Page:Sticker({ Label = "Mine" })
function Kuik.Register(Name, Constructor)
	Controls[Name] = Constructor
	return Kuik
end

--- The building blocks, for anyone writing one.
Kuik.New       = Util.New
Kuik.Text      = Util.Text
Kuik.Tween     = Motion.Tween
Kuik.Spring    = Motion.SpringTo
Kuik.Motion    = Motion
Kuik.Util      = Util
Kuik.Parts     = Parts
Kuik.Scroll    = Scroll.Attach
Kuik.Gleam     = Scroll.Gleam
Kuik.Edges     = Scroll.Edges

--- The white layer: a plate that becomes the thing, a ghost that trails it.
Kuik.Reveal    = Reveal
Kuik.Plate     = Reveal.Plate
Kuik.Follow    = Reveal.Follow
Kuik.Ghost     = Reveal.Ghost
Kuik.Trail     = Reveal.Trail
Kuik.Wipe      = Reveal.Wipe
Kuik.Close     = Reveal.Close
Kuik.Cover     = Reveal.Cover
Kuik.Flash     = Reveal.Flash
Kuik.Row       = Parts.Row
Kuik.Block     = Parts.Block
Kuik.Attach    = Layout.Attach
Kuik.Tooltip   = Parts.Tooltip

--- Showcase ----------------------------------------------------------------

--- Every control the library has, in one window. Built for looking at: if
--- something is broken it is broken here, and anything that fails to build
--- says so in place rather than in the output.
---
---   Kuik.Showcase({ Key = Enum.KeyCode.F8 })
function Kuik.Showcase(Options)
	return require(script.Showcase)(Kuik, Options)
end

--- Screen ------------------------------------------------------------------

function Kuik.Screen()
	return Screen.Get()
end

--- The layer itself, for the two things about it that callers need: how much of
--- the top the platform has taken, and how to cover the whole window in spite
--- of it.
Kuik.Inset = Screen.Inset
Kuik.Cover = Screen.Cover
Kuik.Safe  = Screen.Safe

--- True while a prompt is up.
function Kuik.Blocked()
	return Screen.Blocked()
end

--- Tears down every window, panel and HUD piece this library made, and the
--- blur effects it parked in Lighting.
function Kuik.Reset()
	Screen.Destroy()

	for _, Effect in game:GetService("Lighting"):GetChildren() do
		if Effect.Name == "KuikBlur" then
			Effect:Destroy()
		end
	end
end

return Kuik
Controls/Colour:
--!nonstrict
--- Colour.luau — the colour controls.

local Palette = require(script.Parent.Parent.Theme)
local Util    = require(script.Parent.Parent.Util)
local Motion  = require(script.Parent.Parent.Motion)
local Parts   = require(script.Parent.Parent.Parts)

local Theme   = Palette.Tokens
local Metrics = Palette.Metrics

local New     = Util.New
local Text    = Util.Text
local Corner  = Util.Corner
local Padding = Util.Padding
local List    = Util.List
local Strip   = Util.Strip
local Stroke  = Util.Stroke
local Clamp   = Util.Clamp
local Hex     = Util.Hex
local Round   = Util.Round

local Tween = Motion.Tween

local Block       = Parts.Block
local BlockHandle = Parts.BlockHandle
local Draggable   = Parts.Draggable

local Controls = {}

--- The swatch and hex readout every colour control carries in its top right.
--- Lives in the block's Aside, which is hand positioned and therefore safe
--- from the list layout that would otherwise stretch it down the card.
local function Readout(Built, Value)
	local Slot = Built.Aside or Built.Frame

	local Swatch = New("Frame", {
		Name             = "Swatch",
		Parent           = Slot,
		BackgroundColor3 = Value,
		BorderSizePixel  = 0,
		AnchorPoint      = Vector2.new(1, 0),
		Position         = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0),
		Size             = UDim2.new(0, 34, 0, 20),
		ZIndex           = 3,
	}, {
		Corner(Metrics.ChipRadius),
		Stroke(Theme.White, 0.7, 1),
	})

	local Label = Text({
		Parent           = Slot,
		Text             = Hex(Value),
		FontFace         = Theme.FontMono,
		TextSize         = Metrics.MonoSize,
		TextTransparency = Theme.TextTertiary,
		TextXAlignment   = Enum.TextXAlignment.Right,
		AnchorPoint      = Vector2.new(1, 0.5),
		Position         = UDim2.new(1, -40, 0.5, 0),
		Size             = UDim2.new(0, 60, 0, 12),
		AutomaticSize    = Enum.AutomaticSize.None,
		ZIndex           = 3,
	})

	--- Roblox owns these colours, not the theme, so they must not be repainted
	--- when the theme changes.
	Palette.Release(Swatch)

	return Swatch, Label
end

--- Color. Three channel sliders, RGB.
function Controls.Color(Container, Options)
	local Handle = {}
	local Value = Options.Default or Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)

	local Built = Block(Container, Options)
	local Swatch, Label = Readout(Built, Value)

	List(7).Parent = Built.Content

	local Channels = { { "R", Value.R }, { "G", Value.G }, { "B", Value.B } }
	local Fills = {}
	local Stops = {}

	local function Compose(Notify)
		Value = Color3.new(Channels[1][2], Channels[2][2], Channels[3][2])
		Swatch.BackgroundColor3 = Value
		Label.Text = Hex(Value)

		if Notify and Options.Callback then
			task.spawn(Options.Callback, Value)
		end
	end

	for Index, Channel in Channels do
		local Line = New("Frame", {
			Parent                 = Built.Content,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 14),
			LayoutOrder            = Index,
		})

		Text({
			Parent           = Line,
			Text             = Channel[1],
			FontFace         = Theme.FontMono,
			TextSize         = Metrics.MonoSize,
			TextTransparency = Theme.TextTertiary,
			TextYAlignment   = Enum.TextYAlignment.Center,
			Size             = UDim2.new(0, 12, 1, 0),
			AutomaticSize    = Enum.AutomaticSize.None,
		})

		local Track = New("Frame", {
			Parent                 = Line,
			BackgroundColor3       = Theme.White,
			BackgroundTransparency = 0.82,
			BorderSizePixel        = 0,
			AnchorPoint            = Vector2.new(0, 0.5),
			Position               = UDim2.new(0, 16, 0.5, 0),
			Size                   = UDim2.new(1, -16, 0, Metrics.SliderTrack),
		}, {
			Corner(2),
		})

		local Tint = Index == 1 and Color3.fromRGB(255, 96, 96)
			or Index == 2 and Color3.fromRGB(96, 210, 128)
			or Color3.fromRGB(96, 156, 255)

		local Fill = New("Frame", {
			Parent           = Track,
			BackgroundColor3 = Tint,
			BorderSizePixel  = 0,
			Size             = UDim2.new(Channel[2], 0, 1, 0),
		}, {
			Corner(2),
		})

		Palette.Release(Fill)

		Fills[Index] = Fill

		local Grab = New("TextButton", {
			Parent                 = Line,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			Text                   = "",
			AutoButtonColor        = false,
			Position               = UDim2.new(0, 16, 0, 0),
			Size                   = UDim2.new(1, -16, 1, 0),
			ZIndex                 = 3,
		})

		local Stop = Draggable(Grab, Track, function(X)
			Channel[2] = Clamp(X, 0, 1)
			Fill.Size = UDim2.new(Channel[2], 0, 1, 0)
			Compose(true)
		end)

		table.insert(Stops, Stop)
	end

	function Handle:Get()
		return Value
	end

	function Handle:Set(NewValue, Silent)
		Channels[1][2], Channels[2][2], Channels[3][2] = NewValue.R, NewValue.G, NewValue.B

		for Index, Fill in Fills do
			Fill.Size = UDim2.new(Channels[Index][2], 0, 1, 0)
		end

		Compose(not Silent)

		return Handle
	end

	Compose(false)

	local Result = BlockHandle(Built, Handle, Options)

	Result:OnDestroy(function()
		for _, Stop in Stops do
			Stop()
		end
	end)

	return Result
end

--- ColorPicker. A saturation and brightness field over a hue strip.
function Controls.ColorPicker(Container, Options)
	local Handle = {}
	local Value = Options.Default or Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
	local Hue, Saturation, Brightness = Value:ToHSV()

	local Built = Block(Container, Options)
	local Swatch, Label = Readout(Built, Value)

	List(8).Parent = Built.Content

	local Field = New("Frame", {
		Parent           = Built.Content,
		BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromHSV(Hue, 1, 1),
		BorderSizePixel  = 0,
		Size             = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, Options.Height or 96),
		LayoutOrder      = 1,
		ClipsDescendants = true,
	}, {
		Corner(Util.Radius(Options, Metrics.ChipRadius)),
	})

	Palette.Release(Field)

	--- White across, black down: the standard two gradient stack that turns a
	--- flat hue into a saturation and brightness field.
	New("Frame", {
		Parent                 = Field,
		BackgroundColor3       = Color3.new(1, 1, 1),
		BorderSizePixel        = 0,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0),
		ZIndex                 = 2,
	}, {
		New("UIGradient", {
			Color = ColorSequence.new(Color3.new(1, 1, 1)),
			Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
				NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0),
				NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1),
			}),
		}),
	})

	New("Frame", {
		Parent                 = Field,
		BackgroundColor3       = Color3.new(0, 0, 0),
		BorderSizePixel        = 0,
		Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0),
		ZIndex                 = 3,
	}, {
		New("UIGradient", {
			Rotation = 90,
			Color = ColorSequence.new(Color3.new(0, 0, 0)),
			Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
				NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 1),
				NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 0),
			}),
		}),
	})

	local Marker = New("Frame", {
		Parent                 = Field,
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		AnchorPoint            = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5),
		Size                   = UDim2.new(0, 13, 0, 13),
		ZIndex                 = 5,
	})

	for Index = 1, 2 do
		New("Frame", {
			Parent           = Marker,
			BackgroundColor3 = Theme.White,
			BorderSizePixel  = 0,
			AnchorPoint      = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5),
			Position         = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5, 0),
			Size             = Index == 1 and UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 1) or UDim2.new(0, 1, 1, 0),
			ZIndex           = 5,
		})
	end

	local Strip_ = New("Frame", {
		Parent           = Built.Content,
		BorderSizePixel  = 0,
		BackgroundColor3 = Color3.new(1, 1, 1),
		Size             = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 12),
		LayoutOrder      = 2,
		ClipsDescendants = true,
	}, {
		Corner(Util.Radius(Options, Metrics.ChipRadius)),
		New("UIGradient", {
			Color = ColorSequence.new({
				ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.000, Color3.fromHSV(0.000, 1, 1)),
				ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.166, Color3.fromHSV(0.166, 1, 1)),
				ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.333, Color3.fromHSV(0.333, 1, 1)),
				ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.500, Color3.fromHSV(0.500, 1, 1)),
				ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.666, Color3.fromHSV(0.666, 1, 1)),
				ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.833, Color3.fromHSV(0.833, 1, 1)),
				ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(1.000, Color3.fromHSV(1.000, 1, 1)),
			}),
		}),
	})

	Palette.Release(Strip_)

	local HueMarker = New("Frame", {
		Parent           = Strip_,
		BackgroundColor3 = Theme.White,
		BorderSizePixel  = 0,
		AnchorPoint      = Vector2.new(0.5, 0),
		Size             = UDim2.new(0, 2, 1, 0),
		ZIndex           = 3,
	})

	local function Compose(Notify)
		Value = Color3.fromHSV(Hue, Saturation, Brightness)

		Field.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromHSV(Hue, 1, 1)
		Swatch.BackgroundColor3 = Value
		Label.Text = Hex(Value)

		Tween(Marker, { Position = UDim2.new(Saturation, 0, 1 - Brightness, 0) }, "drag")
		Tween(HueMarker, { Position = UDim2.new(Hue, 0, 0, 0) }, "drag")

		if Notify and Options.Callback then
			task.spawn(Options.Callback, Value)
		end
	end

	local StopField = Draggable(Field, Field, function(X, Y)
		Saturation, Brightness = X, 1 - Y
		Compose(true)
	end)

	local StopStrip = Draggable(Strip_, Strip_, function(X)
		Hue = X
		Compose(true)
	end)

	function Handle:Get()
		return Value
	end

	function Handle:Set(NewValue, Silent)
		Hue, Saturation, Brightness = NewValue:ToHSV()
		Compose(not Silent)
		return Handle
	end

	function Handle:GetHSV()
		return Hue, Saturation, Brightness
	end

	Compose(false)

	local Result = BlockHandle(Built, Handle, Options)

	Result:OnDestroy(function()
		StopField()
		StopStrip()
	end)

	return Result
end

--- Swatches. A fixed set of colours to pick from, which is usually what a game
--- actually wants rather than the whole spectrum.
function Controls.Swatches(Container, Options)
	local Handle = {}
	local Items = Options.Items or {}
	local Value = Options.Default or Items[1]
	local Cells = {}

	local Built = Block(Container, Options)

	New("UIListLayout", {
		Parent            = Built.Content,
		Padding           = UDim.new(0, 6),
		FillDirection     = Enum.FillDirection.Horizontal,
		SortOrder         = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder,
		Wraps             = true,
		VerticalAlignment = Enum.VerticalAlignment.Center,
	})

	local function Render()
		for _, Cell in Cells do
			local On = Cell.Colour == Value

			Tween(Cell.Ring, { Transparency = On and 0 or 1 }, "hover")
			Tween(Cell.Frame, {
				Size = On and UDim2.new(0, 26, 0, 26) or UDim2.new(0, 22, 0, 22),
			}, "toss")
		end
	end

	for Index, Colour_ in Items do
		local Cell = New("Frame", {
			Parent           = Built.Content,
			BackgroundColor3 = Colour_,
			BorderSizePixel  = 0,
			Size             = UDim2.new(0, 22, 0, 22),
			LayoutOrder      = Index,
		}, {
			Corner(Round(Options, 11)),
		})

		Palette.Release(Cell)

		local Ring = Stroke(Theme.White, 1, 2)
		Ring.Parent = Cell

		local Button = New("TextButton", {
			Parent                 = Cell,
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			Text                   = "",
			AutoButtonColor        = false,
			Size                   = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0),
			ZIndex                 = 3,
		})

		Cells[Index] = { Frame = Cell, Ring = Ring, Colour = Colour_ }

		Button.Activated:Connect(function()
			if Handle:IsDisabled() then
				return
			end

			Handle:Set(Colour_)
		end)
	end

	function Handle:Get()
		return Value
	end

	function Handle:Set(NewValue, Silent)
		Value = NewValue
		Render()

		if not Silent and Options.Callback then
			task.spawn(Options.Callback, Value)
		end

		return Handle
	end

	Render()

	return BlockHandle(Built, Handle, Options)
end

--- Gradient. Two colours and a rotation, previewed live.
function Controls.Gradient(Container, Options)
	local Handle = {}
	local From = Options.From or Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
	local To = Options.To or Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 0)
	local Rotation = Options.Rotation or 0

	local Built = Block(Container, Options, Options.Height or 34)

	local Bar = New("Frame", {
		Parent           = Built.Content,
		BackgroundColor3 = Color3.new(1, 1, 1),
		BorderSizePixel  = 0,
		Size             = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0),
	}, {
		Corner(Util.Radius(Options, Metrics.ChipRadius)),
	})

	Palette.Release(Bar)

	local Ramp = New("UIGradient", {
		Parent   = Bar,
		Rotation = Rotation,
		Color    = ColorSequence.new(From, To),
	})

	function Handle:Get()
		return From, To, Rotation
	end

	function Handle:Set(NewFrom, NewTo, NewRotation)
		From = NewFrom or From
		To = NewTo or To
		Rotation = NewRotation or Rotation

		Ramp.Color = ColorSequence.new(From, To)
		Ramp.Rotation = Rotation

		if Options.Callback then
			task.spawn(Options.Callback, From, To, Rotation)
		end

		return Handle
	end

	return BlockHandle(Built, Handle, Options)
end

return Controls
